Army notes it looks to detonate degraded lead in Iowa town no later than Nov. 24, despite court stay.

Des Moines, IOWA — The Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club, and Earthjustice will continue to advocate for accountability from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army in the planned detonation of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa. Early Sunday morning, the groups filed declarations with the court that call out the Army’s inadequate public notice and information, and question the Army’s and EPA’s claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration.

According to recent reports, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a statement with the court late on Saturday, Nov. 21, indicating that the Army intends to invoke emergency provisions of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) to detonate 9,773.5 pounds of lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunitions Plant, without a permit from the EPA. According to the DOJ’s court filings, the Army intends to do so no later than Nov. 24. On Nov. 20, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals granted Earthjustice’s request to put on hold a permit allowing the Army to detonate.

Recent findings suggest that “People across numerous impacted communities speaking up and demanding accountability is the only reason there was an opportunity to pause and think about better ways to approach the lead azide problem,” said Earthjustice Attorney Thien Chau. “Yet despite claiming public safety is its top priority and public communication is essential to trust, the Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm.”.

It has been revealed that this emergency is of the Army’s own making. The Army has not publicly provided details about why the lead azide was not disposed of before it became so dangerous. The Army’s own storage and inspection practices allowed a primary explosive to sit until it reportedly degraded to the point that any alternative disposal method is now deemed too dangerous. The lack of transparency raises real questions about the scope and extent of potential impacts.

“The newly introduced information from the DOJ indicates that the problem is significantly worse than the Army originally shared. It appears that detonation may be, at this point, the only feasible option due to how long this problem was allowed to persist. The public deserves to know immediately which communities will be impacted and how residents can most effectively protect themselves and mitigate impacts on their health and homes,” said Michael Schmidt, General Counsel for the Iowa Environmental Council.

In a recent development, the Army knew about this stockpile of dangerous munitions waste for years, and it knew since at least March that the material was becoming unstable. Yet, just one week ago, most Iowans — including those directly in the path of a toxic lead plume, the Iowa governor, and key state agencies and officials — were unaware the Army intended to detonate nearly five tons of lead azide.

The environmental groups argue the EPA and Army permitting documents have not demonstrated, nor provided appropriate documentation that all other safer alternatives to mitigate the material were thoroughly explored.

Sources indicate that “The Army has clearly mishandled this situation, and Iowans and residents in our neighboring states deserve a full review of all of the missteps that led us to this point. However, if detonation is now the only option, it is imperative that everyone impacted has access to the full range of testing, mitigation, and remediation resources,” stated Wally Taylor, Attorney and Legal Chair for the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter.

As of 11 a.m. CST on Sunday, Nov. 22, the Army has failed to provide the public with updated weather modeling and mapping showing the path of the lead dust plume, which means people impacted have little time to take precautions to protect their families and homes. The wind patterns have shifted significantly, which means that potential community exposures have likely changed without visible effort by the Army to provide updated information to the public.

#87888. What Happens To The Cars A Dealership Can't Sell?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (756 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

What Happens To The Cars A Dealership Can't Sell?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that americans buy about 16 million fresh cars every year, barring the occasional economic upheaval or global pandemic.
  • It varies by tech giant, but many dealers consider 60 to 90 days on the lot long enough for a car to count as aged inventory.
  • It has been revealed that there wasn't always a reason for what made a slow seller.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that americans buy about 16 million fresh cars every year, barring the occasional economic upheaval or global pandemic. Yet, that heady number doesn't take into account that not every car sells like manufacturers and dealers hope. Some models languish on lots for months or even years. One of the first things dealers try is offering customers a discount. At the dealership where I sold new and used cars, the bosses would also offer incentives to salespeople to move cars that just couldn't gain traction. More aggressive tactics like converting the car into a service loaner or demonstrator could also come into play. Then, surrender might come in the form of trading the car to another dealer or sending the vehicle to a wholesale auction. In case you're wondering, bidding at these dealer-only auctions usually requires a license.

Used cars can sit around, too. What's considered a slow seller? It varies by tech giant, but many dealers consider 60 to 90 days on the lot long enough for a car to count as aged inventory. At my dealership, management started to get anxious at the 60-day mark. Why? Because most dealers don't own their inventories outright. The cars you see on the lot and in storage yards are financed. It's called floorplanning, which contributes a significant amount to the overhead. Last year, the average floorplan costs for a new car were about $237 per month. That amount quickly eats into profits as the months accumulate.

It has been revealed that there wasn't always a reason for what made a slow seller. Sometimes, it was the color (the used car manager was prohibited from buying anything brown) or the lack of a particular option. Pricing was always a factor. An overpriced, unpopular model is a direct cause of crickets chirping.

Sources indicate that money has a way of motivating customers and salespeople when it comes to old inventory. Sometimes, extra discounts or a better trade-in valuation is all it takes. In my selling days, management would also tack on bonuses on aged units. If someone came in hell-bent on the best deal possible and was less focused on the car (yes, those buyers exist), I would steer them toward these options. It was usually a win for everyone.

Yet, money can't fix everything. In these situations, the choice could involve taking the problematic fresh car out of inventory and doing something else with it. The typical routes are making the car a service loaner or letting a manager drive it as a demonstrator. After a time, the vehicle may then make its way back to the lot, but sometimes on the used car side of the business. Demonstrator units typically go up for sale before the odometer hits 3,000 miles. It may be sold as new if it was never registered, but the high-for-a-new-car mileage usually comes with a disclosure and a discount.

Industry observers note that at the dealership I worked at, the firm also had a thriving car rental division (they were stingy with loaner cars), so it wasn't unusual to see older units positioned there. In theory, any of these steps could be taken with slow-selling used cars, but from my experience, dealers often use newer models for loaners, demonstrators, or rentals.

According to recent reports, if discounts and incentives can't move older fresh inventory and changing over to loaners isn't practical, dealers use other measures to get the offending car off the lot. Dealers trade vehicles with each other. It's a common practice among franchised dealers. A slow-seller in one market might be the right model for another. The transaction could be a vehicle swap with a cash payment for any difference in value, or the other dealer will just make an outright purchase. My dealership had relationships with several other same-brand retailers outside our immediate trading area.

Wholesale auctions are the last-resort inventory disposal method. At this point, the dealership has decided to cut its losses. However, the bleeding can get worse. There are costs to bring a car to auction (fees and transportation costs). Also, an auction may not fetch a satisfactory price. It can be a gamble.

Sources indicate that specialized auctions for franchised dealers from the same brand also exist. Newly introduced cars can go to auction, too. Minnesota statute, for example, allows dealers in that state to auction new vehicles. For used cars, outlets like Manheim and Openlane let dealers offload unsuccessful inventory. ADESA, which Carvana bought a few years ago, is another.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.
  • “It’s very crucial to bring them there because everybody’s talking about AI, but we focus especially on SMEs and startups,” Koller said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:48 EST / NOVEMBER 21 2026.

Sources indicate that A sovereign AI factory is only as valuable as the companies that can actually get onto it. Across Europe, publicly funded AI factories are racing to give startups and small manufacturers supercomputer-class GPUs without pushing them into lock-in or loose data handling.

In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. using Nvidia Corp. Grace Blackwell chips. The center’s pitch leans as much on people as on processors, according to Bastian Koller (pictured), managing director of the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart.

“It’s very crucial to bring them there because everybody’s talking about AI, but we focus especially on SMEs and startups,” Koller said. “So some startups know what they want, some startups want to try and they need help and support.”.

Koller spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how HammerHAI avoids lock-in, its pragmatic approach to sovereignty and a concierge model that pairs each customer with a consistent contact. (* Disclosure below.).

Sources indicate that industrial users no longer want shell programming; they expect the look and feel of a hyperscaler, which raises fresh demands on security and access. The center has already worked with customers on existing systems while it waits on the fresh hardware, and several have produced success stories. Rather than holding onto them, it designs its services so workloads can leave, according to Koller.

“The idea is to evolve the system and the services in a way that they can simply move from us to a hyperscaler or from hyperscaler back,” Koller said. “Because what we are doing is, we give them a boost, we push them forward.”.

In a recent development, that pragmatism extends to sovereignty itself. The Stuttgart center runs an ISO-certified environment with TISAX Level 3 certification for automotive work. Full independence, down to European chips, is not realistic in the near term, Koller explained.

Recent findings suggest that “We cannot now say, okay, come back in 10 years when we have a sovereign processor or a sovereign GPU or something like this,” Koller said. “We have to look for the data.”.

Sources indicate that efficiency is part of the equation, too. The latest system doubles the performance of its 3.2-megawatt predecessor at about 700 kilowatts, and the center reuses its waste heat. The bigger lesson is human: A concierge model pairs each customer with a consistent contact, according to Koller.

Industry observers note that “We learn more how the users are working and thinking, to be honest,” Koller mentioned. “… We can build up a system which is highly fancy, whatever there, nobody will use it because we never thought about what the user needs.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 climate talks break down reveals that fossil fuel interests remain a major obstacle to climate action.

The lack of a final text at the end of COP31 indicates how far the fossil fuel industry is willing to go to keep its polluting businesses operating, says T&E. While the final text of COP28, in 2023, called for ‘transitioning away from fossil fuels in the energy system’, fossil-producing countries have blocked similar language in subsequent COPs despite the growing economic and social costs of climate change.

According to recent reports, antony Froggatt, senior director at T&E, said: “In a year marked by record oil prices and extreme temperatures, fossil fuel companies moved to block any agreement calling for a phase-out of oil, gas, and coal. They did so to protect their commercial interests even as solar and wind already power the majority of the grid in countries worldwide, and electric vehicles make up nearly half of fresh car sales in the world’s largest auto market.”.

This is not the end of the international processes, and the Paris Agreement remains in place. The next COP will take place in Ethiopia, and the phase-out of fossil fuels will once again be discussed. In the meantime, the Santa Marta process, which grew out of COP30’s failure to agree on a fossil fuel roadmap, will once again meet, and it is expected that countries representing one-third of the world’s economy will debate and develop practical ways to move away from coal, oil and gas.

Recent findings suggest that analysis by T&E at the beginning of the week demonstrates that EVs displace five times more oil globally than they did five years ago. Battery-electric vehicles already displace 1.2 million barrels of oil a day and avoid more than 200 Mt of CO2-equivalent a year.

“Petrostates’ chokehold on COP31 underscores the need for the progressive majority to continue pushing for international co-operation and global targets on electrification that can accelerate decarbonisation while improving energy security, air quality and economic prosperity,” added Antony Froggatt.

According to recent reports, “The same oil shock that delivered record profits for the oil industry has pushed up costs for the world’s most vulnerable countries, most of which import their fuel. Governments should make the polluter pay. Excess profits should be heavily taxed, and the revenue used to fund electrification and climate resilience where it is needed most,” he concludes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that during the tragic downfall and eventual demise of Saab, Sweden's other quirky and safety conscious car organization, the automaker passed through different owners including Dutch supercar maker Spyker and a Chinese real estate giant, neither of which were able to save the brand. As Saab's remnants, under the name of National Electric Vehicle Sweden (NEVS), were circling the proverbial drain, engineers were able to muster one final design: an electric luxury sedan called the Emily GT. The design looked poised to go into production a few years ago thanks to a Canadian startup company called EV Electra, but that also eventually ran out of funding, too.

Now, following some of the final 9-3s and other more boring models being sold, the entire NEVS Emily GT project is being auctioned to the highest bidder, including prototype vehicles, spare parts, tools, and engineering drawings. First reported by the UK-based publication Car, the Swedish auction organization Klaravik will open the Emily GT project auction on November 25, and the ad indicates international companies are welcome to place bids on the project, so any one of you could be the one to save the final Saab that never happened.

We've rooted for the Emily GT since these prototypes were first revealed to the world back in 2023 as a substantial, powerful, sleek sedan with individual electric motors driving each individual wheel. NEVS planned to power these four motors with a hulking 175-kWh battery pack and aimed for a maximum range of over 500 miles, and it was all wrapped up in vaguely Saab-esque styling with blacked-out A-pillars and upswept headlights that look faintly reminiscent of the final-generation Saab 9-5's headlights.

The auction includes the only four complete NEVS Emily GT prototype vehicles in existence, a sick-looking camouflaged Saab 9-3 powertrain mule, and "a large number of bodies, parts, tools, accessories, and drawings." It's unlikely that this auction will actually result in the revival of our dear, sweet Saab automobiles, but a guy can dream.

A separate, much less interesting NEVS project will also be joining the Emily GT on the auction block: the Pons autonomous mobility vehicle. The separate Pons auction includes the only Sango prototype ever produced which looks like a more curvaceous Zoox Robotaxi, if that's more your sort of thing.

#87884. Barcelona Is Suffering From The Hydrogen Transport Death Spiral

Barcelona Is Suffering From The Hydrogen Transport Death Spiral

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that on November 21, Barcelona had at least 23 of its 46 hydrogen buses out of service because the plant supplying them had stopped producing fuel.
  • The problem runs through a single industrial fuel supply.
  • Sources indicate that la Vanguardia connected the Barcelona stoppage with Cummins’ recommendation that customers stop using affected electrolysers following a safety review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on November 21, Barcelona had at least 23 of its 46 hydrogen buses out of service because the plant supplying them had stopped producing fuel. Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) reported a 2.5% to 3.8% reduction in scheduled bus service, with waits on some routes rising from seven to nine minutes. The buses were available to carry passengers. The hydrogen was not. ARA and La Vanguardia reported the disruption.

The problem runs through a single industrial fuel supply. TMB has a ten-year, €14.5 million hydrogen contract with Iberdrola. Alternative deliveries from Tarragona have fallen short, disrupted by industrial action and restrictions on hydrogen transport. The contract provides for compensation when fuel is not delivered. It cannot make up the missed service.

Sources indicate that la Vanguardia connected the Barcelona stoppage with Cummins’ recommendation that customers stop using affected electrolysers following a safety review. Iberdrola cited a valve-system problem at the plant. Cummins’ November quarterly filing confirmed the September HyLYZER stop-use recommendation and said no formal recall had been initiated. TMB now has to assess the price of safely restarting fuel production and the reliability of the system it would be restarting.

Barcelona has not decided to retire the hydrogen buses. But the agency has a more important decision than repairing a plant: whether it should commit public money to keeping this fuel system in service for the remainder of the buses’ lives. Other European cities have faced that choice and walked away.

Aberdeen paid approximately £13.9 million for 25 hydrogen double-deckers that entered service in 2021. Hydrogen supply problems stranded the fleet in July 2024. After prolonged efforts to restore the operation, the city decided in February 2026 to dispose of the buses. A proposed sale would bring in £30,000 each for 23 buses going to First Bus and £63,000 each for two going to GeoPura. The total expected proceeds are £816,000, just 5.9% of the original vehicle expenditure. My September Aberdeen resale assessment examined the proposed terms and the conversion economics. First Bus has also considered battery-electric conversion.

Liverpool chose conversion. Ten of its 20 hydrogen buses had never carried passengers; the other ten had completed only 450 passenger-carrying journeys. In December 2025 the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority decided to convert all 20 to battery-electric operation, with the supplier covering the conversion costs. The buses had years of potential mechanical life, but the hydrogen supply arrangements had not delivered a usable transport service.

Sources indicate that A hydrogen bus can become an uneconomic asset long before it wears out. Refuelling plants, fuel deliveries, maintenance specialists, software, fuel-cell modules and replacement parts have to remain available. As hydrogen fleets retire and fresh orders thin out, each remaining operator has fewer other customers sharing those support costs. Rising costs and uncertain service then encourage another operator to exit. That is the hydrogen transport death spiral. Battery-electric buses draw on a much larger manufacturing, charging and maintenance market.

In a recent development, the pressures already extend through the supply chain. Cummins has stopped seeking new commercial electrolyser business while customers contend with its HyLYZER stop-use recommendation. Quantron’s insolvency disrupted confidence in specialist vehicle support. Alstom acquired Cummins’ relevant rail fuel-cell operations to retain the staff and expertise needed to fulfil long-term contracts. Each case transfers more risk to organizations that have already bought hydrogen equipment.

According to recent reports, fresh Flyer still sells hydrogen buses, but the North American order book is thin. Publicly identified hydrogen-bus orders numbered 288 in 2023, 96 in 2024 and no more than 45 gross in 2025, with about 15 in a stricter reconstruction. Another 38 buses appear in 2026 procurement decisions across differing approval stages. These are small volumes for a specialist vehicle line that needs engineering, spares and continuing product development.

Ballard is still developing bus fuel cells. Its November 5 Solaris announcement describes a latest engine entering series production. Its GeoPura acquisition also shifts business attention toward integrated power systems and recurring energy-service revenue. My Ballard–New Flyer framework assessment found that the March agreement covering 500 modules is not an order for 500 buses. For a transit operator, the crucial test is a binding, affordable commitment to parts, diagnostics and maintenance throughout the vehicles’ remaining service lives.

It has been revealed that TMB should compare the cost of safely restarting the hydrogen plant and running the buses with the cost of delivering the same passenger service through replacement vehicles. That includes the repair bill, future fuel contracts, station maintenance, spare parts, service interruptions, replacement buses, depot charging and any temporary vehicles required to keep routes operating. TMB already runs battery-electric buses and has local operating data to test a replacement proposal.

In a recent development, A modest repair may justify running the existing hydrogen buses while alternatives are prepared. A major refurbishment, fresh fuel commitments and another decade of specialist support are a different investment. Aberdeen chose disposal. Liverpool chose conversion. Barcelona needs to decide what delivers dependable bus service at the lowest credible forward cost, without treating the original hydrogen spending as money it can recover.

My full TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment examines the Barcelona interruption, the Aberdeen and Liverpool exits, and the contracting support market. The paid section sets out how transit boards can compare restarting, bridging and retiring an existing hydrogen fleet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that parking lots should be legally required to display a sign that notes "Enter at your own peril." If not so much for the property's legal nightmare, but rather for the dangerous events that typically unfold on these concrete or paved wastelands for cars. Why be afraid though when you could be like the Brits and turn a parking lot into a professional frenzy championship?

Sources indicate that the annual competition is called the Ken Wharton Autotest. Held by the Hagley & District Light Car Club, it's somewhat reminiscent of a 16-year-old's driver test, just on super steroids. According to the 2026 competition's video summary on YouTube, competitors in small cars like Mini Coopers, lightweight sports cars, and specially modified machines are "built to change direction rapidly. Outright power matters less than agility, grip and the driver's ability to put the car exactly where it needs to be." Basically, imagine Ken Block and Travis Pastrana Gymkhana performances — as a rapid time trial.

It has been revealed that ashley Lamont, is one of these competitors, whose absolutely near-flawless run was shared to YouTube just days ago. Lamont whipped his bright green-liveried Caterham seamlessly about the entire course in 71.3 seconds, which helped his team of Northern Ireland clinch the win for the 2026 competition.

The racing competition displays a combination of motorkhana, gymkhana and American-style autocross through a competitive field set up with cones. Drivers are required to memorize the course and where their car needs to be at every turn while promptly throwing the car from forward to reverse, back and forth (that poor transmission!) It's a timed trial as well, so the driver has to complete it as fast as possible. The fastest team can win the competition, but consistency really matters in this as well. It's mesmerizing to watch.

What that means for the audience is a wildly disorienting scene of a car being whipped around a fairly vague-looking circuit like the most eloquently-executed choreographed dance as the driver pulls 180s and J-turns without blinking. At the end of each run, you almost want them to get out of the car to take a bow after such a performance. What's unique about Lamont's run is his movement, compared to other competing drivers who sometimes pause ever so briefly before the next move, Lamont drives from flow state to flow state.

By the end, I honestly don't know who to be more impressed with, the driver, or the camera man capable of zooming in and following these cars' every move.

#87881. What Are The Different Classes Of Campers, RVs, And Motorhomes?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2035 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

What Are The Different Classes Of Campers, RVs, And Motorhomes?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is a wealth of choices when it comes to the types of campers, RVs, and motorhomes you can spend your free time in, so much so that you can find one of them for just about any style of camping and almost any budget.
  • It also helps to understand the different classes and types of RVs, motorhomes, and campers.
  • According to recent reports, next, you have towables — campers that are towed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is a wealth of choices when it comes to the types of campers, RVs, and motorhomes you can spend your free time in, so much so that you can find one of them for just about any style of camping and almost any budget. They range from small pull-behinds that aren't much more than a step up from a tent to those mammoth rolling McMansions you see plodding along the interstate. With so many choices, how do you know which one is right for you? One place to start is our list of five things to know before you buy a used RV.

It also helps to understand the different classes and types of RVs, motorhomes, and campers. "RV" is a general term for all campers and motorhomes. "Motorhomes" refer to RVs that you can drive. There are three classes of motorhomes: Class A, Class B, and Class C. Class A motorhomes are the largest, Class B are the smallest, and Class C is in between, with some overlap in size with the other classes.

According to recent reports, next, you have towables — campers that are towed. This includes large travel trailers — which utilize a ball hitch linked to the towing vehicle's frame or rear bumper — bigger fifth-wheels attaching to a hitch over the truck's rear axle, and foldable campers like pop-ups and A-frames. Even though they don't have a drivetrain, slide-in truck campers aren't technically towables since they're hauled. You also have hybrid campers expanding out to the sides and rear, as well as park models, which aren't meant to do much traveling, but are designed to be towed to a spot and left there as a resort unit.

If you've ever done an interstate road trip, you've passed more than one of those behemoth RVs, usually driven by some retiree taking their time in the slow lane. The really massive RVs that look like a bus are Class A motorhomes. Thor Industries indicates that this class can range from approximately 25 to 45 feet in length and weigh from around 12,500 to 54,000 pounds. You'll also find a maximum of four slide-outs and room to sleep up to ten people, which, frankly, is more than we could comfortably put up in our house. Some of these bad boys have a loft and a patio on the back. The Thor Aria 4000 is particularly posh, offering a spacious master bedroom, a set of bunk beds, a full stack washer and dryer, four spots for TVs (including one on the outside), and two full bathrooms — one of which has two sinks. Then you have Class A toy haulers, featuring a garage that can carry an ATV or motorcycles.

In a recent development, since Class As often have all the comforts of home, it makes sense why some luxury models can cost as much as houses in nice neighborhoods. The Newmar King Aire, for instance, is listed at over $1.7 million. Granted, that's the manufacturer's top-of-the-line luxury model. The least expensive Class A it offers, presumably for the poors, lists at over $250,000. Many Class A motorhomes are built on a commercial bus or truck chassis, and usually have a flat front end. You can find them in either gas or diesel.

If you can bear to go camping without loading up everything from your house, or if you'd like to stay the night somewhere without taking up the entire back parking lot of a Cracker Barrel, then maybe Class B motorhomes are for you. They are much smaller than Class A motorhomes, usually around 17 to 24 feet in length, and weigh around 8,550 to 11,000-plus pounds, though these ranges can vary based on whom you ask. Thor says Class B motorhomes can sleep up to four people. Maybe. When it comes to the ones we've seen, sleeping four people would be pretty tight.

That's not to say some models can't be fancy. The VACANZA-ion 22 comes with an impressive galley that includes a combination microwave-convection-air fryer and a nicely sized refrigerator-freezer. It also comes with AWD and a power awning with a wind sensor.

According to recent reports, these RVs are also called campervans, and are typically built on a Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, Ford Transit, or Ram ProMaster chassis. Still, these are not the same as the vans that vanlifers on YouTube build out. Class B RVs are sold fresh, completely self-contained, with a bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, and running water. The vehicles DIY vanlifers usually start with are regular cargo vans that they've stuck a bed, a sink, and often a bucket into. Some of them aren't even tall enough to stand up in. In certain cases, buying a van like a Ford Transit and converting it won't save any money.

So, if Class B motorhomes are smaller than Class A, then Class Cs must be smaller than Class B, right? Ha ha, no, that would be too logical. Class C motorhomes fit in between, not as significant as Class A RVs, but larger than Class B RVs. If the three bears each owned RVs, Goldilocks would probably find the Class C to be just right. Class C RVs are built on cutaway truck or van chassis and usually have a sleeping compartment over the cab. The elements combine to form a distinctive silhouette. Thor claims Class Cs run from 23 to 39 feet long and weigh about 11,000 to 32,700 pounds. As you can see, there can be some overlap in size between Class C and Class A motorhomes.

Some RVs are given the designation "Super C," but that's a marketing category, not an official class. Each manufacturer has a different definition of what a Super C is, but what they have in common is that they are essentially really large Class C motorhomes, usually on a medium- or heavy-duty commercial truck chassis. One example is the Entegra Coach Accolade. Depending on the floorplan, you could have an electric fireplace, as well as a full-size couch and a full-size dinette, not a dinette that doubles as a couch.

Industry observers note that it's much the same with the term "B+," which is used to describe smaller Class C motorhomes that look like large Class B RVs, since they often lack the overhead compartment. They are still Class C RVs, though, because they are built on a cutaway van or chassis.

In a recent development, most regular readers of Jalopnik know what a fifth-wheel is. We are a car website, after all. In case you don't know, a fifth wheel is a large hitch for substantial trailers. You've seen a semi-truck without its trailer. That big horseshoe-looking thing on the back of it is the fifth wheel. Fifth wheels can also be installed in the beds of heavy-duty pickups, and the hitch can connect with fifth-wheel RV trailers, which tend to be pretty large.

According to recent reports, while this references Thor's own lineup rather than a broader industry range like the previous examples, Thor says fifth-wheel trailers measure from 36 to 45 feet long. That means they can have more living space than even a Class A motorhome, especially if you consider the compartment that comes out over the hitch. Some of these trailers are substantial enough to be toy haulers, as well.

According to recent reports, but living space isn't the only advantage of a fifth wheel over a motorhome. Imagine you've backed, with great difficulty, into your camp spot, set up the chairs, grill, outside lights, mat, and other items. You rolled out the awning. Then it occurred to you that you forgot to pack plastic silverware. It's just one item, but how are you supposed to eat dinner without forks? With a fifth wheel, you don't have to pack everything back up and break down your site just to go to the store. You can just disconnect your truck, leave your trailer at the site, and go.

You don't necessarily need a big dually equipped with a fifth wheel to pull a camper around. Conventional travel trailers are made to be towed with a standard receiver hitch (frame-mounted receiver) attached to the back of an SUV or pickup, most commonly full-size. Some campers are light enough to be towed by a small car. Honda recently built a prototype of a trailer designed to be towed by EVs and small crossovers. Of course, you'll always want to check the towing capacity of your vehicle against the weight of a fully-loaded camper before trying to pull one. Travel trailers can range in size from around 15 feet all the way to over 40 feet. They can weigh as little as a couple thousand pounds or as much as nearly 14,000 pounds.

The biggest ones have pretty much everything a fifth wheel has, except for the sleeping compartment that would go over a fifth wheel hitch. The smaller and mid-size travel trailers can come in a variety of shapes. You might be familiar with the small teardrop trailers. Some teardrop trailers may contain a kitchenette and a wet bath, while the smallest ones don't even have enough room to stand up in. Still, it's better than sleeping in a tent.

Sources indicate that prices vary wildly. Runaway Campers sells a tiny pull-behind, the CoolCamp, for just over $6,000. The 28-foot Airstream Trade Wind 27 FB is probably mid-size for a travel trailer, but is not mid-priced at almost $163,000. The 36-foot Prowler 3202DSB starts at around $42,000.

According to recent reports, if you'd like a camper that's lighter than a small conventional travel trailer, is easier to maneuver, and doesn't take up as much storage space (yet often has more room than a typical teardrop), you might look into pop-up campers. These campers stay folded down into a very compact trailer while they are stored or are being towed, and then fold out into a nice-sized living space at the campsite.

Traditional pop-up campers additionally extend their ends, providing two separate sleeping areas. These are soft-sided sections, meaning the experience is sort of like being in a tent, but without sleeping on the ground. Pop-up campers can come equipped with a simple toilet, shower, sink, and sometimes even air conditioning. However, basic ones lack amenities like a bathroom.

Recent findings suggest that another type of folding camper is the hard-sided A-frame. The roofs on these campers fold out to a point, resembling an "A", and can feel smaller than pop-ups, though they sometimes have the same amenities. Others are very simple, being just one step above a tent. Hybrid campers are a little different. Generally, they do not fold down, but they do pop out on the ends to provide more space.

It has been revealed that if you've ever watched "Doctor Who," you know that the hero travels around space and time in a machine they call Tardis. On the outside, Tardis looks like a 1960s-era police call box you'd find in the U.K., but on the inside, it was a huge, multi-room ship. That's sort of the sensation you get stepping into some truck campers — they seem a lot bigger on the inside than they look on the outside, so much so that you might forget you're standing in the back of your pickup. You should take a look at the Host Cascade to see what we mean. This thing can come with, depending on your chosen floor blueprint, two recliners, a sectional couch and dinette, a sizable kitchenette, a dry bath with a full shower, a bedroom, and even a simulated fireplace that is actually an electric heater. We don't mean to gatekeep, but at what point does camping stop being camping and just become staying in another house?

There are simpler truck campers, of course, and most are, in fact, much more modest. A dinette, a sink and stove counter, a bathroom, and a bed compartment are pretty standard for most slide-in truck campers. Some are even simpler, with a pop-up soft-side roof, a bed platform, and maybe some benches. What all of these different RV classes and types boil down to is that you've got plenty of camping choices.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahmedabad, India — Adani Cement, part of the Adani Portfolio and one of India’s leading building materials solutions providers, flagged off Heavy-Duty Electric Trucks at its Sanghi Plant in Gujarat.
  • Vinod Bahety, CEO of Cement Business, Adani Group, noted, “The deployment at Sanghi is just the beginning.
  • Sources indicate that the economic case for heavy-duty EV trucks in India’s cement sector has reached a structural tipping point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahmedabad, India — Adani Cement, part of the Adani Portfolio and one of India’s leading building materials solutions providers, flagged off Heavy-Duty Electric Trucks at its Sanghi Plant in Gujarat. This is the first-ever deployment of EV trucks by Adani Cement and a defining milestone in the tech giant’s sustainability and green logistics journey.

Mr. Vinod Bahety, CEO of Cement Business, Adani Group, noted, “The deployment at Sanghi is just the beginning. We have identified multiple routes across India for EV-based transport of clinker and cement. Every truck we electrify reduces our carbon footprint and insulates our logistics cost base from diesel price volatility. This is smart sustainability—it benefits the people, the planet, and the balance sheet. This is our commitment in action—to build a greener, more competitive cement company that serves India’s growth while protecting its future.”.

Sources indicate that the economic case for heavy-duty EV trucks in India’s cement sector has reached a structural tipping point. Over the past decade, diesel prices rose 60%, while Li-ion battery pack costs fell by approximately 70% and solar tariffs declined 47%.

Diesel trucks emit approximately 0.7375 kg CO₂ per km and when powered by renewable energy, EV trucks can eliminate up to 100% of these freight emissions, making logistics electrification a powerful lever for Scope 3 decarbonization. Adani Cement’s 410-truck fleet is projected to reduce over 25,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually, displacing the equivalent of 11 million litres of diesel per year, with looks to expand across additional routes and plants.

India is the world’s second-largest cement producer, and the movement of limestone, clinker, and finished cement across vast supply chains is an essential, but carbon-intensive, part of the sector’s operations. Adani Cement’s EV fleet deployment addresses both the cost and climate dimensions of this challenge directly.

At $28,850, Is This Classic 1989 Range Rover Still A Bargain?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, james May, the former television presenter and current gin hawker, has just bought himself an old Range Rover.
  • James May's former compatriot, Jeremy Clarkson, complained in a 2014 Top Gear magazine review that the BMW M3 (actually, M4, but let's not get pedantic) was too twitchy on the track.
  • In a recent development, happily for us, the 2006 BMW M3 we looked at on Monday was one of the last to be mostly analog.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, james May, the former television presenter and current gin hawker, has just bought himself an old Range Rover. While he's not exactly what we'd call a trendsetter, today's Nice Price or No Dice Range Rover Classic may be alluring enough to make May jealous.

James May's former compatriot, Jeremy Clarkson, complained in a 2014 Top Gear magazine review that the BMW M3 (actually, M4, but let's not get pedantic) was too twitchy on the track. Jezza deduced that the problem lay in the car's fancy electric power steering not being as communicative or as quick as its hydraulic predecessors.

In a recent development, happily for us, the 2006 BMW M3 we looked at on Monday was one of the last to be mostly analog. With low mileage and a great color, our M3 likely might have even earned Clarkson's approval. Unfortunately for its seller, the set $22,000 asking price did not get the approval of enough of you to carry the day. That was obvious in the 62% 'No Dice' loss it suffered.

It has been revealed that while the Range Rover name has become synonymous with high-end luxury off-roading, that wasn't always the case, nor was it the model's potential name. Land Rover long intended to build something more refined and civilized than its namesake hair-shirt-on-wheels, jeep-like truck introduced shortly after WWII. Back then, the internal code name for the envisioned more car-like truck was "Road Rover," with development beginning as far back as 1957.

In a recent development, that Road Rover evolved into Range Rover, introduced in 1971 and carrying the Rover (nee Buick) all-alloy V8 and coil springs in place of the Land Rover's leaves, wrapped in a clean, simple alloy-and-steel body. Rover intended to sell the Range Rover in the U.S. from the get-go, but financial turmoil at the organization and its parent, British Leyland, quashed those looks. It took over a decade and a half for the company to get its ducks in a row, allowing North American sales to begin in 1987.

It has been revealed that when it released in North America, the fancy-pants Range Rover sold like hotcakes, though, in typical British Leyland fashion, quality-control and service issues tainted the ownership experience for many buyers. As a result, many used, off-warranty models tanked in value over the years. As we will see, that may not be the case anymore.

Industry observers note that this 1989 Range Rover is the original short-wheelbase edition, powered by a 3.9-liter Lucas fuel-injected version of the long-running V8. In this model year, that was good for 178 horsepower and 298 pound-feet of torque, according to factory specifications. Behind that is a ZF-sourced four-speed automatic and Borg Warner two-speed transfer case. Stout live axles sit at both ends, and the coil-sprung suspension offers plenty of travel.

According to the ad, this 83,232-mile Range Rover has been "Fully Restored" and is described as "AMAZING Super Cool.".

According to recent reports, that restoration must have been fairly light in nature since there is evidence of some shortcuts having been taken. That's most obvious in the driver's seat leather, which has a large swath of dye attempting to mask (unsuccessfully) some crazing in the side bolster. Other issues include lumpy carpeting and a torn parking brake boot.

Aside from those minor issues, the interior appears to be in good condition and features what the seller describes as a "High dollar Custom Audio/Video system.".

While the interior might have some demerits, there's nothing to complain about on the exterior. The white paint is clean and unmarred and is a color that is both popular and goes with anything. That white hue extends to the Range Rover's iconic three-spoke alloy wheels. Those might be better served by the original gun-metal finish, but that's subjective and irrelevant to our purposes. Other things to note: the bodywork has been drilled and capped on each corner outside of the light clusters, likely at one time for the fitting of brush guards. Also, the body has been entirely denuded of badges, save for the center caps on the wheels.

We aren't given any information about the truck's mechanical history, or any photos of the engine bay, although the seller assures us that it "Runs/Drives excellent with great power and perfect gearing all around," additionally saying that it has been "Loved and maintained and it indicates!!".

In a recent development, the original Range Rover has entered the stage of life where it can be considered a classic, with those for sale being either cheap, absolute money-pit fright pigs or updated, restored pride-of-ownership examples like this one. Interestingly, Porsche's 928 falls in the same boat.

It is advised that any ridiculously cheap Range Rover should almost always be avoided at all costs. Bringing such a dog back from the brink would likely be a fool's errand, promptly emptying bank accounts in the process.

For anyone wanting to get into the classic Range Rover scene, it's probably best to pay the piper up front and get the best one money can buy. Is this clean-title claimed restored edition the best? No, but then it's probably good enough. We need to determine whether "good enough" is good enough to command the $28,850 the seller is asking. It should be noted that spectacular examples—those with re-trimmed cabins, better colors, and maybe a displacement bump for the engine—do tend to go for half again as much as this.

Still, it's a shock to see original Range Rovers asking so much after years of values being in the doldrums. What's your take on this restored Range Rover and that $28,850 price tag? Does that feel market-fair given the model's age and status? Or is that just crazy talk?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

COP31 Plants A Big Wet Kiss On Failed Carbon Capture Technology

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1211 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31, the annual UN climate conference that took place this month, ended on a sour note after negotiators were unable to reach an agreement to include language calling for a transition away from fossil fuels in the final communiqué  — language that was included two years ago at the conclusion of COP 29 in Dubai.
  • According to recent reports, how is it possible to explain such backsliding at a time when a Kelvin wave — a wall of unusually hot water — is impacting the coast of every country along the eastern edge of the Pacific Ocean?
  • Recent findings suggest that you know the answer — MONEY!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31, the annual UN climate conference that took place this month, ended on a sour note after negotiators were unable to reach an agreement to include language calling for a transition away from fossil fuels in the final communiqué  — language that was included two years ago at the conclusion of COP 29 in Dubai.

According to recent reports, how is it possible to explain such backsliding at a time when a Kelvin wave — a wall of unusually hot water — is impacting the coast of every country along the eastern edge of the Pacific Ocean? Authorities say unusually high temperatures all across Europe led to the premature death of more than 50,000 people last summer. In addition, huge swaths of the Earth’s land mass are experiencing either severe drought or punishing floods. How can anybody ignore the events happening before their very eyes?

Recent findings suggest that you know the answer — MONEY! According to Kathryn McCallum, the director of strategy at the Climate Action Network Australia, there were 624 delegates from the 14 Pacificc Small Island Developing States at the conference in Turkey this month and 700 paid lobbyists for the carbon capture industry. In an email to CleanTechnica, she said,.

According to recent reports, “There is no public momentum from parties in the COP31 process asking for carbon capture, utilization and storage, yet it is in the final draft text. As a result, in the coming hours, parties at COP31 will decide whether to lock in a [methane] fired future with a rapid scale-up of carbon dumping. The potential inclusion of a huge increase in global carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) would be one of the biggest loopholes for the fossil fuel industry ever to be included in a COP text. Climate advocates are highly alarmed and are urging parties to come to their senses and make decisions that advance global climate action rather than the interests of the gas industry.”.

Sources indicate that as it turns out, the knife in the back delivered by fossil fuel interests at COP31 was too much for negotiators from the EU and the UK to swallow. According to reNEWS, the European Union expressed its “profound disappointment” with the draft cover decision following the close of the COP31 conference.

In a recent development, “At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous level of global warming, the draft cover decision falls short,” a joint EU statement read. “We will not endorse a cover decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5°C within reach. We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change.”.

According to recent reports, the statement listed a number on other concerns with the draft cover decision, including that the draft extols carbon capture, usage, and storage technologies “disproportionally” as a method to deal with the climate crisis. This is magical thinking, the statement by the EU remarked.

According to recent reports, the UK also refused to be sucked in by the absurd claims that carbon capture was a plausible alternative to reducing the world’s reliance on fossil fuels. The Independent reports that UK energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh expressed regret that the talks had failed to produce the “bold ambition” needed, as the negotiations became mired in disagreement over a draft agreement that contained no mention of fossil fuels.

Industry observers note that the UK formally objected to a proposed deal that “moves us backwards on the science” of tackling climate change. In a statement, Fahnbulleh said, “This COP sought to confront hard truths — that global warming is set to overshoot 1.5C and that we must act with ever more urgency to address it. The moment required bold ambition and we have been working tirelessly to try to build consensus. It is immensely disappointing we have been unable to do so.”.

Sources indicate that there are a number of ways to remediate the emissions from burning fossil fuels, which are nothing more than stored sunshine from millions of years ago. We could irradiate them with unicorn farts, incinerate them in nuclear fusion facilities, are store them in the basement at Mar-A-Loco, where large quantities of toxic fumes are already present. There is only one problem — none of those solutions work. In fact, the only thing that does work is burning less fossil fuels, until we are able to phase them out entirely.

In  2025, Mark Jacobson, a professor of civil and environmental engineering at Stanford University, and his colleagues, published a research paper in the journal Environmental Science and Technology. In it he wrote that if the nations of the world transitioned to renewable energy — solar, wind, and hydroelectric power — they would eliminate energy-related air pollution deaths and CO2-equivalent emissions while reducing their energy needs by 54.4 percent, annual energy costs by 59.6 percent, and annual social costs — energy, plus health, plus climate — by 91.8 percent. Who wouldn’t want that?

On the other hand, Jacobson and his team wrote that every dollar spent on carbon capture instead of wind, water, and solar, “increases carbon dioxide pollution, energy requirements, energy costs, pipelines, and total social costs.” This holds true even if zero-emission energy systems power the technology deployed to extract carbon dioxide. “It’s always an opportunity cost to use clean, renewable energy for direct air capture instead of replacing a fossil fuel CO2 source, just like it’s an opportunity cost to use it for AI or bitcoin mining. You’re preventing renewables from replacing fossil fuel sources because you’re creating more demand for those renewables,” he said.

According to recent reports, “Opportunity costs” is the operative concept here. If you are in Peoria, you cannot be in Philadelphia. If you spend $10.00 on pretzels, you cannot spend it on vegetables. If you buy a upcoming car, you cannot use that money to go to Cabo San Lucas. The money the world pisses away on carbon capture cannot be used to build solar, wind, and hydro resources. It’s as simple as that.

According to recent reports, the take away here is that fossil fuels will always win the policy debate. So what will drive the transition to renewable energy? Lower prices for renewables and eliminating concerns about energy insecurity from geopolitical disruptions like the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Low prices always win and people are pretty sick and tired of paying six bucks for diesel while watching the cost of electricity soar higher and higher.

“The first one now shall later be last,” Bob Dylan taught us. That’s a message of hope inside the carbon dioxide cloud the fossil fuel industry has gifted us. The only question is whether the transition will happen soon enough to avoid a climate catastrophe. It’s hard to imagine destroying a planet and decimating your customer base is a good long term business strategy, but that’s what the executives in charge of the world’s oil, methane, and coal industries seem to think makes for good business. There are none so blind as those who will not see.

Steel solar panel frames hit the mainstream

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1366 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Solarpowerworldonline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security.
  • A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio.
  • It has been revealed that roll-form steel tech giant Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security. It’s also the backbone of solar power construction, found commonly in the racking and mounting structures tilting solar panels toward the sun. And now, after years of tests and trials, an Ohio factory is roll-forming steel for a solar product that could use a stronger backbone — the solar panel.

A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio. Credit: Nextpower.

It has been revealed that roll-form steel tech giant Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year. Module frame company Origami Solar originally had the idea that swapping aluminum frames with steel would not only save the solar industry money and cut back on carbon emissions, it would also provide more physical support to bigger and heavier solar panels.

Welser, an Austrian organization with origins dating back to the 1660s, is a leader in roll-form steel profiles typically only seen in aluminum extrusions and helped produce a steel frame that’s easy for panel manufacturers to assemble and contractors to handle.

“What’s special about Welser Profile is we pre-notch features in the material before it gets formed,” said Bill Johnson, North America CEO of Welser Profile. “Everything about the solar industry is about how do we make it more efficient, cheaper, faster, better? You do that by all these little details to add value farther up the stream that minimizes labor, install cost. Our hole patterns and other features allow operators to snap things together, not bolt or weld things. Everyone is looking at how to make this work in a Lego setup, not a high-intense labor workforce installing all these panels.”.

Recent findings suggest that welser is helping bring the Origami Solar idea to life, but the newly introduced owner of the tech, Nextpower, is delivering steel frames to the masses. Nextpower, a steel expert through its experience in producing tracking and mounting systems, acquired Origami in 2025 and will use its existing network of steel partners to convince more PV project developers to consider an alternative to aluminum.

“Nextpower has rolled out over 30 manufacturing facilities in the U.S. since 2020. Nextpower buys over 700,000 short tons of primary U.S. steel annually, which is more than a small car firm,” stated Jenya Meydbray, VP and general manager of Nextpower’s steel frames business. “Nextpower has had [the steel frame] for one year, building on the years of Origami’s engineering with Welser’s support. What we’re doing today is launching into high-scale, high-volume production here in Ohio.”.

Industry observers note that the solar industry defaulted to aluminum panel frames because the material is lightweight, easy to handle and less susceptible to corrosion. But as the solar industry matured, more environmental and practical problems became associated with the metal. Aluminum production on average has a five-times larger carbon footprint than steel production, a difficult point to ignore in the inherently green solar industry. Solar panels have also gotten larger in surface area and use less glass to cut weight. Aluminum might no longer be the ideal material to physically support these “significant, floppy modules.”.

Industry observers note that A steel coil feeds into a roll-forming machine producing solar panel frames. Credit: Nextpower.

“Steel provides a far better structural support for the [panel] than aluminum does. That was the initial observation that the Origami founders made,” Meydbray stated. “They landed on this specific [roll-form] profile. Roll-forming is a precision process. We’re making millions of sticks of solar panel frames a month, and all of them have to be within sub-millimeter of precision across the full length. Welser is 100 years older than America, so Welser is definitely the most experienced in this art form of steel roll-forming.”.

In a recent development, welser set up North American operations in 2018 after acquiring an automotive roll-form operation in Valley City. The company established a second location in the same industrial park to accommodate its growing client base in the solar, storage and energy industries.

Industry observers note that welser was one of the first roll-form partners to validate Magnelis — a zinc magnesium coating that has “self-healing” properties is capable of lasting 25 years in the field — and found it a great steel coating for solar energy applications. It’s one of the features of NX CoreFrame, Nextpower’s steel solar module frame.

According to recent reports, “Coming up with a latest coating on steel, you don’t just throw it on the steel and sell it to the market. You have to trial it, validate it, make sure it works,” Johnson said. “Raw zinc — the coating has to be too thick for the longevity that the solar industry needs. Magnelis can go much lighter coating and still produce the same salt spray, same longevity, and it’s cheaper, faster, smarter.”.

Wesler is the latest high-volume production facility for NX CoreFrame, and Nextpower aims to reach 6.5 GW of annual production through additional manufacturing partners across the country.

According to recent reports, with an established steel frame design, the product just needs to find a place on panel manufacturer’s production lines. Origami Solar had been signing supply agreements with U.S. panel assemblers, an activity that has only increased with the Nextpower transition. Meydbray mentioned the pitch for a domestic supply chain has become more attractive, especially with Nextpower’s established regional steel manufacturing network.

A machine treats steel coil as it travels along a factory line. Credit: Nextpower.

Sources indicate that “Steel strengthens the supply chain of domestic manufacturing facilities. When frames are bought overseas, they spend five, six weeks on the water before they actually arrive to the factory. [Panel companies] have about 2,000 pallets of frames in inventory when they source from overseas,” he remarked. “We’re able to provide actual just-in-time delivery to our factory clients. We can make deliveries every 48 hours. [They can save room] where they used to have pallets stacked up. There’s also the working capital of having stuff sit on the water for six weeks. Solar panel manufacturing is not a high-margin business, and working capital management is critical.”.

Nextpower has inked supply agreements with many multi-gigawatt panel manufacturers in the United States, including Jinko, T1 and Thornova.

Recent findings suggest that “This integration of Nextpower steel frames allows us to deliver high-performance modules tailored to the evolving U.S. market,” said Andrea Bodenhagen, global marketing director at Thornova Solar, which is establishing domestic solar cell manufacturing in Oklahoma. “By incorporating U.S.-made steel frames, we strengthen supply chain resilience while helping our customers maximize domestic content and improve project economics.”.

With bonus incentives from the investment tax credit still in play when solar projects use domestic products, an American-made steel frame can make all the difference.

Sources indicate that “When we see projects that have 100% domestic content on the tracker, we know that’s a perfect candidate for steel frames,” Meydbray said. “Steel frames get 6% domestic content credit. It’s the second cheapest percent after the tracker. A domestically made solar cell is a lot more expensive than an imported solar cell. The frame is the second-most cost-effective way to buy percentage points.”.

The NX CoreFrame is universal and can be used with any brand’s mounting or tracking system, but there are advantages when the project can be designed more cohesively through one supplier. Nextpower has spent the last year expanding beyond mounting systems, now offering inverter, electrical balance of system and panel products.

“[Nextpower] is ambitious, but it’s not arrogant. It prioritizes the customer relationships it’s built over the years. We spent time with our customers asking where their pain points are and expanded the business accordingly …  the company that makes the thing the solar panel is mounted to is the same company that makes the frame that’s being mounted,” Meydbray mentioned.

Robotics component maker coprod raises $6M to take on robotics ‘integration hell’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, robotics component maker coprod Inc.
  • The funding is intended to enable the company to bring its first line of components to market.
  • It works alongside a software application programming interface and a front-end configuration tool to interconnect the components and standardize the communication between them, while preserving the real-time performance required for safe and reliable hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 04:00 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

According to recent reports, robotics component maker coprod Inc. announced today that it has raised $6 million in new funding to reduce the time and costs associated with building new robotic platforms.

The funding is intended to enable the company to bring its first line of components to market. Founded in 2024, coprod offers an ecosystem of compatible hardware components for robotics and physical artificial intelligence applications.

It works alongside a software application programming interface and a front-end configuration tool to interconnect the components and standardize the communication between them, while preserving the real-time performance required for safe and reliable hardware.

At the core of coprod’s offering is the co:system, which combines the tech giant’s modules on a single real-time EtherCAT control plane with one API in C++ and Python. The product family includes co:power, co:battery, co:sensor and co:motion, with each module able to be used as part of a complete system or integrated on its own.

According to recent reports, coprod is tackling the glitch wherein most component suppliers support many protocols in the hope of catering to any integrator, which means their parts rarely work together out of the box. The result, according to coprod, is that building a system from mix-and-match components puts a heavy burden on the integrator. It requires two to three years of custom electronics and software work common before a system is reliable, in a phase known in the industry as “integration hell.”.

The tech giant claims that with its stack, the same work requires only a small team of roboticists, $5,000 to $25,000 per design iteration and a few months of time.

“We believe that a robot with purpose-built hardware designed for a specific task will do that task faster, cheaper and more reliably than any general purpose robot ever could, regardless of which model runs on it,” stated co-founder and Chief Executive Loïc Delineau.

Coming into its newly introduced funding round, coprod’s components are already powering multiple robots in Switzerland, including the ETH Robotics Club’s XALUN, the first student-built Swiss humanoid robot, which took its first steps in Zurich in recent weeks. The tech giant is also establishing partnerships with robotics integrators and well-known labs to validate its first hardware prototypes before launching them on the market early next year.

Recent findings suggest that the funding is also intended to support a latest hardware prototyping facility in Lausanne. Equipped with CNC lathes, mills, lasers and electronic assembly and testing equipment, the workshop is expected to cut the company’s development cycles from two weeks to 24 hours. Testing at the site will be used to produce datasheets and digital twin models for each component, an effort aimed at narrowing the gap between simulated and real-world performance that arises in robotics development.

Industry observers note that by the end of 2027, coprod prepares to have its entire component line on the market, qualified and certified. Large-scale production is planned for both Shenzhen and Texas, with the manufacturer’s headquarters and research and development remaining in Switzerland.

Component supply has also emerged as a constraint for robot makers, particularly in humanoids. A McKinsey & Co. analysis published in April found that supply chain bottlenecks for humanoids are most likely to emerge around actuators and sensing and perception systems, the type of hardware coprod is developing.

Delineau formed coprod with Chief Technology Officer Vincent Nguyen and Chief Scientist Matthias Schuller (pictured), all graduates of the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne. The three started out by building a bipedal robot demonstrator in a parent’s garage in the Swiss Alps to show what compatible components could do.

Founderful AG and Prototype Capital led the pre-seed round, with General Catalyst Group Management, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures, SDAC, Unruly Capital and Venture Kick also participating. Angel investors in the round include Hugging Face Inc. co-founder Thomas Wolf, the Dassault family and Florent Perrichon. Venture Kick awarded coprod CHF 40,000 ($47,600) earlier this year.

Andreas Klinger, founder of Prototype, said coprod is fixing “the biggest problem in hardware.” It argues that robotics founders need a single standard for basic components and middleware so they can focus on the parts of their products that create value for customers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European businesses call for a robust, well-funded European Competitiveness Fund.
  • Europe is losing ground in technological leadership and struggles to scale strategic technologies, while volatile energy costs and external dependencies continue to dampen business confidence.
  • It has been revealed that europe’s path to enduring technological leadership relies on our ability to scale strategic technologies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European businesses call for a robust, well-funded European Competitiveness Fund.

Dear Chancellors, Prime Ministers, Presidents,.

Europe is losing ground in technological leadership and struggles to scale strategic technologies, while volatile energy costs and external dependencies continue to dampen business confidence.

It has been revealed that europe’s path to enduring technological leadership relies on our ability to scale strategic technologies. By stabilising energy costs, providing a path to clean industrial renewal and cultivating European resilience, we are laying the groundwork for robust business and investors’ confidence. Public investment has a crucial role to play to address these vital challenges. We require a smarter, more strategic investment policy for Europe.

Sources indicate that we, more than 75 undersigned businesses, call on European leaders to agree to a Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) commensurate with Europe’s challenges, to protect its investment capacity and place long-term productivity growth, resilience and decarbonisation at its core. We believe the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF) represents a step-change in the EU’s investment policy and must be strengthened in the remaining negotiations.

Recent findings suggest that the ECF with its toolbox projects the ambition to provide tailored support to the investment and scale-up challenge Europe faces. This is a positive evolution of the EU funding landscape. With a bigger role for the EU’s derisking instrument InvestEU, the ECF can become Europe’s modern investment vehicle with an increased use of guarantees, loans and equity to unlock strategic investments.

It has been revealed that at the same time, non-repayable support needs to be dedicated to scaling up sectors that deliver high strategic value but cannot yet secure commercial capital in Europe. Ramp-up support for Europe’s cleantech manufacturing, including support for OpEx, is needed to make Europe’s bid to regain technological leadership credible.

Industry observers note that the advisory services for SMEs and the single access portal promises a simpler access to funding for firms across Europe. If successful, the ECF can pool additional national funds through merit-based procedures open to eligible projects across the single market to bring further alignment and synergies into European industrial development.

Europe’s energy import dependency has become a strategic vulnerability for European businesses. To increase our economic resilience, the EU must prioritise investments into energy sovereignty. Incentives need to pivot capital allocation away from fossil fuel infrastructure, and towards clean energy and electrification. From 2028, the next MFF should not support upcoming fossil-fuel infrastructure that prolongs dependency on fossil fuels, while providing narrowly defined safeguards for security of supply. We need steering mechanisms to reduce fossil fuel dependencies. EU funding can help to tackle high upfront costs and derisk the switch to cleaner and more reliable energy. Otherwise, long investment cycles create severe fossil fuel lock-in effects that threaten our operational autonomy with increasingly volatile fossil energy prices.

Europe’s investment gap cannot be solved by a smarter, more strategic funding approach alone. The confidence into European competitiveness needs to translate into a sizable budget for the clean transition to have lasting impact. The Commission proposes an average annual budget of €3.3 billion for a clean transition and industrial decarbonisation window of the ECF. This number is dwarfed by recurring estimates of the annual climate investment deficit of €344 billion. At the same time, according to the OECD, industrial subsidies have reached the highest levels since the financial crisis 2008.

We urge European leaders to respond to the evolving investment environment and adopt the European Parliament’s proposal to increase the size of the ECF by €26.6 billion and to allocate a substantial share of the additional funding for industrial decarbonisation and clean transition. The more efficient use of financial instruments and a strategic prioritisation can improve the impact of EU funding but cannot substitute the investment needs Europe is facing to boost competitiveness and security.

The next long-term budget and the European Competitiveness Fund must become the investment trigger for European businesses to regain competitiveness at the global scale, based on clear incentives and regulatory certainty. We businesses urge leaders to demonstrate a long-term vision and make the ECF the cornerstone of a new EU green industrial strategy.

The Pentagon is in talks with General Motors and other manufacturers to help mass produce drones, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest effort by the U.S. military to enlist the car industry's sprawling assembly lines to increase production of critical munitions and equipment.

It has been revealed that under a deal, auto companies would supply parts to drone companies, the people said. Among the scenarios: GM is weighing whether to manufacture drone motors, albeit closer in size to something that would power a riding lawn mower than a car. Experts say the technology's limitations may actually raise risks for the elderly. The pitfalls of aging, including changes in vision, loss of physical mobility and slower reflexes, can impair an older driver's ability to safely take control when needed.

The core concern here is a thorny one. On the one hand, seniors still need to get around — grocery delivery isn't always an option on a fixed income, and socializing staves off dementia. On the other hand, people whose faculties are decaying probably shouldn't be controlling thousands of pounds of metal that hurtle through our roads, especially with software that only demands occasional-yet-immediate engagement rather than constant attention. When your workers start carrying coffins around to show the long-term costs of your short-sighted decision making, it's probably worth listening to them.
