📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) is an interesting piece of legislation. It is getting a ton of support from the solar sector, but it is heavily opposed by environmental organizations.

In a recent development, following the passage of BAAJA in the US Senate the other day, Tim Pawlenty, CEO of the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA), stated the following: “America is now one step closer to lower energy costs, more clean energy and a more reliable electric grid. Senators Lee, Capito, Heinrich, and Whitehouse deserve tremendous credit for advancing this bipartisan bill.”.

The organization adds some more detail and why it thinks this is such a good piece of legislation: “SEIA analysis shows that BAAJA could unlock 167 gigawatts of additional solar capacity between 2028 and 2035, bringing solar to over 18% of U.S. electricity generation by 2035. The analysis finds that the bill’s reforms could reduce cumulative power sector CO2 emissions by approximately 20% and avoid $54 billion in public health damages.”.

Recent findings suggest that that sounds very appealing, doesn’t it? Why wouldn’t we want that?

Well, the Sierra Club argues the bill goes in quite the opposite direction. The storied organization states the following: “While a rogue president is waging a war on clean energy, the Senate rushed a deeply flawed bill that furthers the buildout of fossil fuels, strips away power from communities and Tribes, threatens our clean water and public lands, and endangers wildlife. The House of Representatives has an equal voice in the legislative process. They must reject the Senate’s fast-tracked bill and demand debate and consideration to deliver for the people, not corporate polluters and Donald Trump. The American people made a clear call merely weeks ago: our elected leaders must address soaring costs and a corrupt system that prioritizes corporate polluter profits over our health, our wallets, and our future.”.

According to recent reports, it seems the matter is that BAAJA would make it much easier to put up power plants, skipping all kinds of environmental protections. That is why Republicans support it in the first place — they are always keen to plow through environmental protections. The reason SEIA supports it is clear enough — the organization is just thinking about solar power plants and looking at the potential for more growth in the industry, especially considering the fact that solar is now typically the cheapest option for latest power capacity and has been dominating new installations.

It has been revealed that so, the question is: would BAAJA really disproportionately support solar power, or would it lead to a lot more fossil fuel power plants and an edge to the old, dirty power technologies? Can the legislation be both good and bad, or is someone getting this wrong?

Stellanis Confirms Nearly All Its Racing Programs Are Dead

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (369 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peugeot might have major racing victories in three different centuries, but that heritage wasn't enough to save its Le Mans Hypercar program.
  • Industry observers note that stellantis stated it intends to "refocus its motorsport activities and resources on customer racing and high-performance vehicle development." Amid the firm's dire financial situation, CEO Antonio Filosa set a goal early this year of $6.6 billion in cost savings by 2028.
  • There were two silver linings to Stellantis' decision.

Peugeot might have major racing victories in three different centuries, but that heritage wasn't enough to save its Le Mans Hypercar program. Stellantis declared on Monday that it's pulling the plug on all its factory motorsports programs, confirming last week's reports. The automotive giant won't fully shutter the motorsport division, hoping to still generate revenue from customer racing. The only projects to avoid the axe were its North American subsidiary's revived NASCAR efforts under the Dodge and Ram brands.

Industry observers note that stellantis stated it intends to "refocus its motorsport activities and resources on customer racing and high-performance vehicle development." Amid the firm's dire financial situation, CEO Antonio Filosa set a goal early this year of $6.6 billion in cost savings by 2028. The decision was sudden for the programs. Peugeot planned to compete with an updated 9X8 in next year's FIA World Endurance Championship and had already begun testing the fresh prototype. With Alpine's previously revealed departure, this means there will be no French manufacturer in the top class of the 2027 24 Hours of Le Mans.

There were two silver linings to Stellantis' decision. First, the company will be continuing its customer racing programs. Second, the company's two Formula E teams will be allowed to contest the upcoming season. Citroën and Opel collaborated in developing new cars for the debut Gen4 campaign. These 800-horsepower machines will get a single season in the sun (or rain) before getting sent to the scrap heap. It's a similar situation to what happened to Lancia's WRC2 program, with the Ypsilon Rally2 HF Integrale running its maiden season this year before Stellantis pulled the plug.

As much as some auto executives champion the "win on Sunday, sell on Monday" mentality, the exposure of being in a motorsport series only truly exists if you're competing in the front half of the field. Using Formula 1 as an example, Aston Martin and Cadillac might as well not exist to TV cameras unless their cars crash or get lapped by the leaders. Saving the Peugeot 9X8 program would be a hard sell for anyone because LMH went five years without winning a WEC race or finishing a Le Mans podium.

#87865. The LiTime Lares K1 Expandable Plug & Play Kitchen Backup — CleanTechnica Tested

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1233 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

The LiTime Lares K1 Expandable Plug & Play Kitchen Backup — CleanTechnica Tested

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1233 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I spent 35 years in the Tampa suburbs, so I pay attention to backup power when a storm  is coming.
  • Industry observers note that liTime debuted the Lares K1 in the US on October 20, 2026.
  • Sources indicate that the inverter puts out 2,000 watts continuously and 4,000 watts of surge power for one second, as a pure sine wave at 120 volts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I spent 35 years in the Tampa suburbs, so I pay attention to backup power when a storm  is coming. Last year I tested the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 portable power station for CleanTechnica. That unit is meant to be carried around. The LiTime Lares K1 is different: a plug-in kitchen backup battery you leave in place and hook up to a refrigerator and also use to power your small kitchen appliances. First I’ll go through the specs and how it compares with a portable station like the Elite 100 V2, then I’ll give my test results.

Industry observers note that liTime debuted the Lares K1 in the US on October 20, 2026. It is a split system: a slim inverter charger paired with a separate 2,304 watt-hour LiFePO4 battery (51.2 volts, 45 amp-hours). You can add up to four batteries, which brings the total to 9,216 watt-hours. The battery is rated for 4,000 cycles, and LiTime backs it with a 5-year warranty.

Sources indicate that the inverter puts out 2,000 watts continuously and 4,000 watts of surge power for one second, as a pure sine wave at 120 volts. Adding batteries does not raise that output. You just get more runtime. There are two AC outlets, one on each side of the inverter. I did not see any USB ports listed.

Sources indicate that you can charge it at up to 1,500 watts from a wall outlet and up to 800 watts from solar (12 to 60 volts). Combined input is capped at 1,500 watts. LiTime does not put a charge time on the main product page. If you divide 2,304 watt-hours by the 1,500-watt wall input, you get about 90 minutes from empty to full. That is a rough estimate. Charging usually slows down as you get close to 100%, the same way an EV does, and their FAQ later puts the theoretical time at about 1.7 hours if you figure 90% charging efficiency.

Sources indicate that the inverter charger weighs about 10.1 pounds. LiTime does not list the battery weight, but I weighted it after I took it out of the packaging and it was about 52 pounds. With the floor stand, the two modules stood up together are 20.47 inches wide, 30.71 inches tall, and 3.94 inches deep. It runs at about 40 decibels (which is very quiet) and switches over to battery in 10 milliseconds or less. It has a touchscreen, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.0, and the LiTime app, plus a time-of-use mode so you can charge off-peak.

The price on LiTime’s site is $1,099.99, shown as $100 off. US preorders opened October 20, 2026, and when I checked, estimated delivery was November 24 to 27.

According to recent reports, liTime calls this “space-based” home backup. Instead of trying to power the whole house, you protect one room, in this case the kitchen. You plug the system into a wall outlet and plug the fridge into the K1. No electrician and no panel work. LiTime estimates about 24 hours of backup on a large side-by-side refrigerator (while I got a bit more than that in my testing) that uses about 2 kilowatt-hours a day, or about 99 hours with four batteries if the fridge is the only load. Depending on the load, it can also run a microwave, an air fryer, a toaster, or a coffee maker for a basic meal. Just don’t try to run them all at once. You can run two smaller loads at once, but a large load like a microwave or air fryer needs to be run by itself (you can keep your refrigerator plugged in too). LiTime notes to allow for compressor startup if you also want to run one of those at the same time.

You can wall-mount it, stand it on the floor, or lean it against a wall, with the two modules together or apart. It comes with mounting hardware and two connection cables, 0.25 meters and 1.5 meters (about 10 inches and 5 feet). The battery housing is steel, and LiTime says the metal finish is meant to suit a kitchen. The inverter is rated IP20, so it stays indoors. LiTime says separating the inverter from the battery cuts down on heat transfer, which they claim helps the battery last longer. I have not measured that.

For a plug & play system, this is a new product category. There have been portable generators available for years that could be used for camping or appliance backup, but having a product tailored to a specific room is a new concept. The comparison they offer is this one-room approach versus a whole-house battery system, the kind that usually needs panel work and that will cost you about 10 times as much.

Recent findings suggest that you can use this for camping or travel, but it isn’t built for it. With split modules, wall-mount hardware, only two AC outlets, and no USB ports, this is built for a permanent kitchen install, not something you toss in the car for a weekend trip.

Industry observers note that I used my old Kill-A-Watt meter to have an independent measure of the draw on the battery from the refrigerator. During the test, I opened the refrigerator less than I normally would, but still opened it about 10 times.

Sources indicate that next I wanted to test it with my small kitchen appliances. First, one at a time; then, several at once. It is rated at 2000 watts continuous, but it should be able to surge up to 4000 watts for 1 second.

Notice that it pulls 2510 watts from the battery, but the load is only 2290 watts. Where did the other 220 watts go? That must be used by the inverter to convert DC to AC.

After 35 years of Tampa storm seasons, I’ve learned that the fridge is usually the first thing you worry about when the power goes out. The LiTime Lares K1 is built for exactly that. In my testing it kept our large side-by-side GE refrigerator running for almost 26 hours on one battery, a bit longer than LiTime’s own estimate of 24 hours. It then shut off cleanly to protect the appliance. Recharging from the wall took about 3 hours, with 80% back in about 2 hours.

It also handled my small kitchen appliances well. The air fryer, coffee maker, and refrigerator ran together at about 2,200 watts, a little over the rated 2,000. When I added the toaster to push it past its limits, it briefly put out about 3,140 watts and then dropped back to about 2,130 watts without shutting down. The app also highlighted about 220 watts lost in converting battery power to AC, which is worth keeping in mind when you estimate runtime.

It does have limits. There are only two outlets, no USB ports, and the battery weighs about 52 pounds, so this is a permanent kitchen install, not a camping generator. Adding batteries gives you more runtime, but not more output.

At $1,099.99, with no electrician or panel work needed and a 5-year battery warranty, the Lares K1 is an affordable way to protect your food and still cook a basic meal during an outage. It costs about a tenth of what a whole-house battery would. If kitchen backup is what you care about most, it’s well worth a look.

#87861. If You Thought The Cybertruck Was Ugly, Get A Load Of This EV On Rails

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1207 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

If You Thought The Cybertruck Was Ugly, Get A Load Of This EV On Rails

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the ill-fated Tesla Cybertruck has been roundly excoriated for its dumpster-adjacent profile, but it looks pretty good compared to the EVs rolling out of the shop at the Missouri-based startup Intramotev.
  • Intramotev surfaced on the CleanTechnica radar back in 2023 with two retrofit products.
  • While the battery packs in each TugVolt have a limited range, that’s more than enough to accomplish a good day’s work including “first mile” loading duties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the ill-fated Tesla Cybertruck has been roundly excoriated for its dumpster-adjacent profile, but it looks pretty good compared to the EVs rolling out of the shop at the Missouri-based startup Intramotev. However, looks are not everything. Intramotev is on a mission to chase diesel fuel off the nation’s nation’s rail freight system, and its “TugVolt” autonomous electrified freight cars get the job done, aesthetically pleasing or not.

Intramotev surfaced on the CleanTechnica radar back in 2023 with two retrofit products. One is the ReVolt, a battery pack that can be slotted onto existing railcars hauled behind a locomotive, with the aim of saving diesel fuel. The other, more interesting retrofit is the TugVolt, an autonomous, electrified system that enables railcars to go about the business of hauling freight on their own, without a locomotive.

While the battery packs in each TugVolt have a limited range, that’s more than enough to accomplish a good day’s work including “first mile” loading duties. Once loaded up, they can hitch a ride on locomotives for long-distance travel, then split off to unload.

Industry observers note that in addition, a freight yard that hosts a full complement of autonomous railcar EVs would require little, if any, participation from diesel-powered switcher locomotives. In addition to hauling its own freight, each TugVolt can also operate as a switcher, ferrying conventional railcars into position behind a locomotive.

The technology also has significant implications for decarbonizing highway freight as well. The closer an electric railcar can get to its destination, the less need there is for a diesel-fueled truck to pick up the slack. In particular, Intramotev is focusing on captive or short line routes, many of which have seen their rail traffic shrink in the face of competition from the trucking industry.

Industry observers note that intramotev has been rather busy over the past three years. In one particularly interesting development, in June Intramotev lent a TugVolt to a US Army Reserve Training exercise at the Camp Shelby Joint Forces Training Center in Mississippi, billed as the largest training exercise in the history of the Army Reserve.

“Soldiers, according to Intramotev, trained on and operated the TugVolt system under tech giant supervision throughout the exercise and promptly became proficient with the technology, a detail that matters because military rail operations have traditionally required specialized rail crews, a category of personnel the Army has struggled to maintain at sufficient strength given how infrequently large-scale rail movements occur outside major deployment exercises,” reports the independent news and analysis organization Defence Blog.

As noted by Defence Blog, the exercise went off script when railcars loaded with military supplies arrived at the site. However, with their training freshly in hand, the participants were able to deploy the TugVolt to organize the incoming railcars for unloading.

It’s no surprise to find Intramotev in Texas, too, considering the state’s reputation as a hot EV market. On November 3, the organization expanded its ongoing relationship with Watco, a holding company specializing in short line railways.

It has been revealed that the fresh arrangement calls for TugVolt to pull zero emission switcher duty at a to-be-named industrial facility in Seadrift, Texas. As noted by Railway Age, the Texas assignment adds to Intramotev’s EV footprint in the US, which also includes Michigan as well as the Army demonstration in Missouri, and a forthcoming agreement in Kentucky.

Railway Age further notes that in April, Intramotev lent itself to electrification efforts in Austria. That’s a particularly significant development because the client is ÖBB, the national railway of Austria, making it the first deployment of TugVolt technology under regulation, in addition to Intramotev’s first overseas client.

The agreement is also significant considering ÖBB’s sprawling footprint in Europe, consisting of more than 1,000 freight trains ranging across 18 countries every day.

Even more significant, at least from a policy perspective, is a $16.3 million grant from the Federal Railroad Administration branch of the US Department of Transportation. US taxpayers will shoulder the bulk of the cost-sharing arrangement, which is designed to model best practices for introducing EVs into the nation’s railway system. The project is hosted by the Columbia Terminal Railroad, a city-owned, 21.4 mile line that links two cities in Missouri, Columbia and Centralia.

“The project will deploy autonomous railcars on the line to produce the first documented safety record for autonomous railcar operation and create a workforce training curriculum,” FRA emphasizes.

“The proposed project was selected for Project Development, Final Design, and Construction and involves research and workforce development activities to conduct a phased autonomous rail technology and short-line infrastructure modernization program,” FRA elaborates, further noting that the EV project “aligns with the selection criteria by improving system and service performance,” with the ultimate goal of enabling freight to run more frequently and, ultimately, autonomously.

It has been revealed that of note, the grant of up to $16 million or so is part of a $2.3 billion railway CRISI modernization package, with CRISI being short for Infrastructure and Safety Improvements. Among other purposes, CSRISI “provides a Federal funding opportunity to “mitigate congestion at both intercity passenger rail and freight rail chokepoints to support more efficient travel and goods movement.”.

Citing Intramotev official Don Soffer, the local news organization News Tribune notes that “more than 600 short lines in the U.S. have declined in use in recent decades due to their relative inefficiency.”.

“Cross-country hauling is more profitable for companies, whereas short lines require very large hauls to justify the quick trip. The Columbia Terminal Railroad (COLT) does not operate on a set schedule, instead hauling whenever enough goods are collected,” the News Tribune continues.

Given that context, if the CSRISI grant is not a decarbonization program for short line railways and associated highway traffic, I’ll eat my hat. It’s also worth noting that practically the entire locomotive fleet of the US runs on a diesel-electric platform, meaning electric motors powered by an on-board generator. While fossil energy is still in play, the diesel-electric configuration is more energy efficient than sending fleets of diesel trucks onto the nation’s highways.

The nation’s trucking industry has also been wrestling with an ongoing driver shortage, providing further motivation to move more freight onto rails, EVs or not.

Stay tuned for updates on that Missouri project. FRA revealed its selection for Project Development, Final Design, and Construction in October, so there are still steps to take before the TugVolt begins running.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, circling back around to that Army demo in June, more likely than not the hookup with the US DoD will not be a one-off. The Army has been notoriously slow to adopt EVs, and last year’s sharp U-turn in federal energy policy did not help. Still, the Army has been sending out EV signals through its use of new “anti-idling” kits for ground vehicles, alongside a new contract with the US branch of the firm Rheinmetall for a fleet of crewless hybrid cargo haulers. Again, looks are not everything….

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The weeks surrounding the Thanksgiving holiday are some of the busiest travel days of the year in the United States.
  • It has been revealed that A coastal flood advisory has been issued for the Pacific Northwest and parts of Northern California, and there's at the moment a nor'easter storm that looks like it will bring heavy rains, winds, and coastal flooding to the entire East Coast over the course of Wednesday and Thursday.
  • The National Weather Service determined that the nor'easter storm strengthening off the southeastern coast could undergo rapid cyclogenesis and become a bomb cyclone by Thanksgiving day.

The weeks surrounding the Thanksgiving holiday are some of the busiest travel days of the year in the United States. This year, AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday November 24 and Monday, November 30, and it projects that 72.8 million of those Americans will be making that drive by car. That's actually a slight drop from last year's result of 73.1 million travelers, but AAA notes travelers in major metropolitan areas could still expect to see more than double the normal traffic congestion. We think that may even be a conservative estimate, given that weather forecasts across the country tell a stormy story.

It has been revealed that A coastal flood advisory has been issued for the Pacific Northwest and parts of Northern California, and there's at the moment a nor'easter storm that looks like it will bring heavy rains, winds, and coastal flooding to the entire East Coast over the course of Wednesday and Thursday. The mayor of San Francisco even posted a video to social media urging people to avoid unnecessary travel, saying, "If you don't need to, please don't travel into the city. We always want visitors, but these are special circumstances." We got all your wet weather driving tips to help folks prepare for the Super El Niño a few months ago, so feel free to revisit that if you can't avoid driving in stormy conditions.

The National Weather Service determined that the nor'easter storm strengthening off the southeastern coast could undergo rapid cyclogenesis and become a bomb cyclone by Thanksgiving day. It's also expected to bring powerful winds with gusts of over 50 mph along the coast and 40 mph inland. The most significant effects are expected to impact the mid-Atlantic and Northeast, so be sure to check the weather forecast in your area before making your elderly grandparents brave treacherous roads.

Industry observers note that west Coast travelers should be aware of the impact of potentially record-high king tides as well as a storm that's expected to bring rain, high-elevation snow, and dense fog from San Francisco all the way up the coast to Southern Washington. This king tide is expected to amplify the already elevated sea levels that have been affecting the West Coast thanks to the Super El Niño's higher water temperatures, potentially causing a surge of more than eight feet in San Francisco Bay. Waves are also expected to become dangerously large, reaching sizes of 20 to 30 feet on Wednesday. Federal experts say San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK), two of the largest airports in California's populous Bay Area, will flood this week from the huge tides. If you've been looking for an excuse to avoid the holiday chaos and stay home to play more GTA, just blame the weather forecast and order takeout.

#87857. 90 Upcoming Vehicle Models Were Just Introduced in Colombia’s Largest Automotive Exhibition. 55 Were Electric.

90 Upcoming Vehicle Models Were Just Introduced in Colombia’s Largest Automotive Exhibition. 55 Were Electric.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The last two weeks, the future was on display in Bogota’s Automobile Hall.
  • Sources indicate that this Hall is Colombia’s largest and most notable Automotive Exhibition, and since 2023 (17th edition, held after a hiatus of 5 years), it has heralded the unstoppable tide of EVs progressively taking over the national market.
  • EVs have been gaining ground since, with more of them arriving every year, and in the latest iteration of the Automobile Hall, we’ve reached a point of no return: EVs make up a majority of the newly revealed models arriving in the country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The last two weeks, the future was on display in Bogota’s Automobile Hall.

Sources indicate that this Hall is Colombia’s largest and most notable Automotive Exhibition, and since 2023 (17th edition, held after a hiatus of 5 years), it has heralded the unstoppable tide of EVs progressively taking over the national market. Back then, despite EVs making up less than 3% of the market, EVs were already present and relevant in the Automobile Hall, with the Changan Lumin being a particularly bright star.

EVs have been gaining ground since, with more of them arriving every year, and in the latest iteration of the Automobile Hall, we’ve reached a point of no return: EVs make up a majority of the newly revealed models arriving in the country. Or to be specific: out of 90 arrivals, EVs account for 55!

32 brands brought fresh electric or plug-in hybrid cars to showcase in Bogota’s Automobile Hall. Even though most of them (unsurprisingly) are from China, we still find presences from 7 European and 2 Japanese brands here — all will be listed at the end of this article with their respective models.

Most of these models arrive at very competitive pricing, many times undercutting their direct gasoline and diesel competition, and with ever-improving specs — by reasonable standards, most of these cars should be able to make at least 350 km on Colombian roads, making them quite appealing options even for people who travel regularly.

Colombia’s EV market share has been growing in 2026, reaching 20% — or almost — every month since March. But with this EV avalanche (or EV-lanche), I think it’s inevitable that we will see that number go up in the months to come — though how fast exactly, I leave to you to debate.

And no, you were not the only ones to notice that there are exactly zero (0) arrivals from US brands. Tesla was of course present, but with nothing upcoming (though they did present the Cybercab at a later date than I attended), other than Tesla, US brands are either too small or too focused on gas-guzzlers to bother even trying to compete.

Note: all prices mentioned here include taxes, but registration and insurance may not be included.

I will start with the non-Chinese EVs, because, well, they’re fewer.

Sources indicate that the most crucial model here, by far, is the Renault 4 e-Tech. People outside this country probably don’t know that the Renault 4 was built here for 22 years, becoming the most affordable car for decades and a symbol of the Colombian middle class. Nicknamed the “Colombian Car” and the “Loyal Friend,” the Renault 4 has a place in the hearth of most Colombians, and, as such, the R4 e-Tech was one of the most visited cars in the entire exhibition.

Because of this, it’s certain that the car will have some buyers. But at 100 million COP (€26,000, $28,500), it’s a hard sell, particularly when the hatchback segment has stabilized somewhere around $20,000 for Chinese models. Nostalgia has a price for sure, but not that many people will be willing to pay $8,500 for it.

The BMW iX3 was also present in the hall, and I must admit it’s a very compelling and impressive car, but at 300 million COP ($85,400), there are not a lot of buyers that will be interested.

From the European side, other than Renault and BMW, we have the Cupra Terramar and the Mini Cooper SE Paul Smith Edition, both around 160 million COP (€41,700, $45,500). So, quite expensive for their segments, even though I find the Terramar a very beautiful car. The Porsche Cayenne is of course expensive beyond anything seen prior, and the Volvo EX60 has not confirmed pricing yet. As for Stellantis, it’s betting on its two vans, somewhat expensive but still viable, and it has the Opel Crossland EV, which has been on the market for a while but is now discounted to 90 million COP (€23,400, $25,600), meaning it’s one of the most competitive non-Chinese EVs available.

Regarding the Japanese, the Toyota BZ4X (already present) and the RAV4 PHEV (just arriving) are of course important players, but at 220 million and 270 million COP respectively ($62,600 and $76,800), they won’t sell more than a trickle of units. The Nissan Frontier Pro has the same price as the BZ4X, and, to be fair, I didn’t even notice it was available until I left the Hall.

Paradoxically, the most competitive non-Chinese EVs all come from a brand with zero arrivals: Kia. With its EV2 starting at 90 million COP and its EV3 at 120 million COP ($23,400 and $34,100), Kia has the closest prices to any Chinese competitor and can at least rely on the brand’s popularity to keep some of the market.

With that out of the way, let’s look at the Chinese arrivals, or at least some of them, as there are too many to mention.

Recent findings suggest that you can see the full list of models at the end of the article. Here I will focus on those I think will make the most impact in the market.

According to recent reports, first, one of my favorite EVs: the all-mighty Chery ICaur V23. In a previous article I mentioned how surprising its low range was … but I must admit I judged it rashly. I mean, that thing is huge. I really expected it to be much smaller, and thus I understand why it can barely edge a 360 km range (WLTP) despite a sizeable 81 kWh battery. When you’re built like a small tank, you can expect to get the range of a small tank, no surprises here.

According to recent reports, but the great selling point for this car is its price: 85 million COP for the 4×2 version and 105 million COP for the 4×4 version ($24,100 and $29,900). We’re talking a fully off-road capable SUV for the same or less than a Renault 4 or a Corolla. Truly impressive, and an example of EV innovation in segments that many other OEMs have not dared enter, assuming they are lost to the ICEV competition.

BYD also surprised by bringing a new Sealion RWD, armed with a 70 kWh battery and aimed directly against the Model Y. At 115 million COP ($32,700), this car is $1,500 cheaper than the Model Y RWD while having a larger battery and better range. It seems the Chinese giant wants to start getting back some market share a year after the US brand took the market by storm. Better late than never I guess.

BYD is also bringing the EREV Leopard 7 under its own brand (BYD Ti7), but at 225 million COP ($64,000), it will certainly not be a best seller, even though it will probably give the likes of Toyota and Land Rover a run for their money.

Industry observers note that now, my dear readers, I hope you will forgive me here, but even though I actually went to the Hall to take a look to the XPeng Mona L03 specifically, it seems I got distracted by the robot and the drone-licopter, and thus this is the picture you’re getting … because I forgot to take one of the L03. Regardless, the XPeng L03 is also pointing directly at Tesla, arriving at 115 million COP ($32,700), the same price of the entry-level Model 3, except the L03 provides full self-driving capabilities for this price, to the extent that XPeng can provide that of course. This car (available in BEV and PHEV versions) and the BYD Sealion are poised to bring a significant challenge not only to Tesla, but to the entire ICEV ecosystem, which is having evermore competition in its bread-and-butter segments by the month.

There are currently 6 subcompact entry-level SUVs fighting in the 80-to-95 million COP segment: the Chery Omoda E5, the MG S5, the Dongfeng Vigo, the Faw Bestune Joy, the Changan Nevo Q05, and the Ora 5.

Industry observers note that I chose the Ora 5 to represent the segment because it offers the largest battery (58kWh, vs 50kWh for all the others) and, as of the Automobile Hall, the lowest price for the entry-level version, at only 73 million COP (USD $20.800). This is a true bargain, making it the cheapest available SUV of any powertrain by quite some distance, and a very compelling option for budget-oriented buyers. It remains to be seen if this price will remain after the Hall.

In a recent development, going by specs alone, I believe the JMEV GSX to be the best value-for-money vehicle right now available in the Colombian market. This SUV boasts an impressive 70 kWh battery with 500 km WLTP range for a mere 90 million COP ($25,600). The only thing against it is that JMEV (JMC) is quite a small brand and has not gained traction in this market, or in any other that I know of.

In Colombia, this minicar has taken the place that belonged to the Wuling Hongguang in China, and more recently belongs to the Chery QQ Ice Cream — that of a (barely) highway-capable minicar that may seat four, or two plus your groceries, but that will fit in any spot and can be parked wherever you may find a square meter available. Available with a brand latest 18.1 kWh battery, the Faw Xiaoma 2.0 remains the most affordable “true” car in Colombia at 40 million COP ($11,400).

It’s worth noting that Faw has failed to gain traction in the Colombian market, and it clearly wanted to change that in this Hall, as it brought an entire armada, with its N09 Sedan available for 100 million COP ($28,300) as its flagship car.

In a recent development, aside from minicars (like the Xiaoma above), the Dongfeng Box deserves a mention for being the cheapest car in the hatchback segment at 65 million COP ($18,500). With its 42 kWh battery, it can reasonably travel long distance with the current infrastructure. I’ve ridden in both this car and the Geely EX2, and, frankly, the EX2 has a higher quality feel, but this one is slightly cheaper, and no doubt this will bring some buyers.

It has been revealed that at a price of only 75 million COP ($21,350), the Foton e-Wonder mini-truck provides full price parity with diesel versions and opens the possibility of electrification for the owners of smaller companies. At 1-ton carrying capacity, it’s a very compelling vehicle, even if its 40 kWh battery remains limited for long-distance operations.

Recent findings suggest that of course, this list would not be complete without the most affordable “real” car here (so, not minicars included, sorry Xiaoma!). The Jac E10X is a city-car available for 60 million COP ($17,000), and even though it looks good and has decent quality, it has never sold well because JAC is not a very popular brand, and because its 30 kWh battery lacks capacity for making even medium-distance trips without having at least some range anxiety.

In a recent development, well, this is it. My apologies for the fans of Arcfox and Leapmotor — both are very important brands arriving in the country, but Arcfox lacks recognition and prices are a bit over the competition (they are a luxury brand, but that may not convince people who don’t already know them) and Leapmotor only brought EREVs, and as you may have seen, I focused on BEVs in the very long Chinese list.

My conclusions are probably quite predictable. China is leading and by quite an advantage, the Koreans are not too far behind, the Europeans are trying to make a comeback, the Japanese are making a symbolic (but useless) stand, and the Americans — other than Tesla — didn’t even bother to show up.

It’s hard to believe only three years have passed since Bogota’s Automobile Hall of 2023, when the Changan Lumin was the star and when we were celebrating going over 2% market share. Back then, EVs were still expensive, charging infrastructure was much more limited, and the mainstream was firmly on the pure-combustion side, with hybrids making some inroads.

Now, after the EV-lanche we’re seeing, it seems that EVs are now fully in the mainstream, with lower prices and better specs than ever before. EV sales will keep growing fast, and I expect the market to tilt even more to the side of zero-emissions transportation in the coming months. 30% BEV market share is now well within sight.

For those of you who want to look at the full list of arrivals, here it is below. BEVs are in bold, PHEVs and EREVs are in regular.

Arcfox T5, T1, S5; Avatr 11, 7; BAIC X55; BYD Sealion RWD, Ti7 (Leopard 7), Atto 8; Deepal S09; Denza Z9 GT, B5; Dongfeng 7, 8; Farizon V7E, F3E; Faw Xiaoma 2.0, Joyee N09, Joyee S08; Foton E-Tunland; GAC Aion UT 2027, S7; Geely Monjaro EM-I, Starray EM-R; GWM Tank 700, ICaur V23, V27; IM IM6; Jetour G700, T2; JMEV GSX; Leapmotor B10, C10; Lynk & Co 2, 1, 8, 900; MHero II; Rox Motor 1; Xpeng L03, L03; Zeekr 007GT, 001FR, 9X.

BMW iX3, iX5, i7; Cupra Terramar; Mini Cooper SE Paul Smith; Peugeot E-Partner, Peugeot E-Expert; Porsche Cayenne; Renault R4 E-Tech; Volvo EX60.

Nissan Frontier Pro, Toyota RAV4.

Latest Update: 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda For Sale With 58,000 Miles Shown Is Racing Royalty With A Wild History

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (802 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Special is subjective — even when it comes to cars.
  • Recent findings suggest that every once in a great while, one of these special Mopar muscle cars comes up for sale.
  • Industry observers note that you might not expect a 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda to rack up race wins in France, but this 'Cuda did just that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Special is subjective — even when it comes to cars. A car that is special to you might just be junk to somebody else. Sorry to burst your bubble, but not every car can count itself among the unicorns and truly special automotive special editions. Then again, other cars are special, full stop. Cars with the sort of presence that makes the little hairs on the back of your neck stand at attention. Understandably, most of us don't often get to see such cars, like the Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda. Massive V8 power and an even bigger personality promptly established the short-lived E-Body Hemi 'Cuda as a muscle car mainstay.

Recent findings suggest that every once in a great while, one of these special Mopar muscle cars comes up for sale. But seldom does one with this sort of record head to the auction block. This is not a Hollywood car, nor was it celebrity-owned. No, this 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda has a racing rap sheet longer than your arm, teeming with victories and championship wins. Better yet, the 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8-powered racing legend racked up its impressive record as a primary factory-backed race car for Ecurie Chrysler in France, of all places. This is one well-traveled 'Cuda. Now, the esteemed asphalt-kicking American ambassador and its 58,000-mile odometer are back in the U.S. of A. and up for grabs courtesy of Bring a Trailer.

Industry observers note that you might not expect a 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda to rack up race wins in France, but this 'Cuda did just that. Henri Chemin, the Chrysler France competition director at the time, drove the car in many Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) and Fédération Française du Sport Automobile (FFSA) events. Chemin managed nine victories in 1970, 16 wins in 1971, and seven victories in 1972. Jean-François Mas took the wheel in 1973, winning 12 times in 1973. This Hemi 'Cuda's last recorded victory was the handiwork of Jean-Claude Géral, who drove the muscle car to victory at the 1974 hillclimb event in Charnizay. All said and done, the 'Cuda claimed 45 Group 1 wins and three FIA championships between 1970 and 1974.

So, what state is the car in today? For starters, the restored-and-retired racer packs a 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8. That Hemi replaced the 'Cuda's original mill during the 1971 season. Should the next owner want to set up a display, the sale includes the original engine block, as well as extensive documentation, photos, a Simca en Compétition racing book, and Chemin's press clippings. A Hurst pistol-grip shifter commands the 'Cuda's four-speed manual transmission, while a Shaker hood and air dam help the old Mopar look the part.

Sources indicate that in keeping with its racing DNA, the old Plymouth features a roll cage, Simpson harnesses, and a white-and-blue racing livery. Other features include 15" Rally wheels in a complementary white hue, body-colored bumpers, front disc brakes, a wood-rimmed steering wheel, an ATL fuel cell, and a dual exhaust system with Flowmaster mufflers.

In a recent development, we don't have to tell you that racing is dangerous — for both driver and machine. Duh, right? Well, at the Brides–Méribel hillclimb event in 1970, the Ecurie Chrysler Hemi 'Cuda met with a motorsport disaster of its own. Piloted by Chemin, the 'Cuda's power steering failed, causing the car to crash into a ravine. The crash was as bad as it sounds. Ecurie Chrysler deemed the Plymouth's body shell beyond repair. So, the racing team's engineers and mechanics salvaged everything they could, including the original engine, much of the drivetrain, the gauges, and the seats. They then transplanted it all into a replacement E-body from a 440 Six-Pack 'Cuda that Chemin had brought into France with the original factory-backed car.

According to recent reports, want this one? You're going to pay for it. As of this writing, the high bid for the Ex-Ecurie Chrysler France 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda is $110,000. Now, stock and well-preserved Hemi 'Cudas routinely net six-figure sums when they go up for sale. Don't believe it? This 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda with 31,300 miles that we reported on last month sold for $176,000 on Mecum. Add a factory convertible configuration into the mix, and a third-gen Hemi 'Cuda has the potential to cross the block for seven figures. After all, just 12 factory rag-top Hemi 'Cudas rolled off the line as 1971 models, making the classic Plymouth a 'Holy Grail' of muscle cars.

There's plenty of space for this motorsport Mopar to sell for big bucks. We just hope someone buys this tenured racing machine and lets it off its leash from time to time. It would be a shame for this one to spend too much time locked away from view with an odometer reading under 60,000 miles.

Toxic Port Pollution Costs Europe €2.5bn A Year In Health & Environmental Damages — Study

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (565 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest research reveals a single ship emits, on average, as much toxic sulphur at port in a year as 19,300 cars, leaving taxpayers and hospitals to pay the hidden cost of shipping pollution.
  • Commercial ships docked in European ports inflict €2.5 billion a year in societal and environmental costs, according to new research by T&E.
  • Instead of plugging into the electrical grid when they dock, thousands of commercial vessels run diesel generators around the clock to power onboard systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest research reveals a single ship emits, on average, as much toxic sulphur at port in a year as 19,300 cars, leaving taxpayers and hospitals to pay the hidden cost of shipping pollution.

Commercial ships docked in European ports inflict €2.5 billion a year in societal and environmental costs, according to new research by T&E. While upcoming EU port rules will cut at-berth damages by 40% by 2030, most vessels remain exempt. Previous research has shown that residents living close to a commercial harbour already face significantly higher risks of cardiovascular and respiratory mortality¹. Tightening port pollution rules would save society billions and protect the health of port communities, notes T&E.

Instead of plugging into the electrical grid when they dock, thousands of commercial vessels run diesel generators around the clock to power onboard systems. These idling engines release harmful pollution directly into neighbouring coastal and port communities. Analysis of Europe’s 100 largest ports indicates that Rotterdam is the most polluted with costs at €350 million, followed by Antwerp (€220 million), Marseille (€120 million), Hamburg (€120 million), and Genoa (€110 million).

It has been revealed that according to the report, removing loopholes in the EU rules would save Europe €1.56bn in health and climate costs. Under current EU rules, outlined in the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), only large container ships, ferries and cruise ships are required to plug into dockside electricity sockets, meaning oil and gas tankers, bulk carriers, car carriers and other cargo ships are left out entirely. Requirements to connect should be progressively extended to all ship types in the upcoming review to cut emissions and grant ports the necessary long-term predictability.

Eloi Nordé, shipping policy officer at T&E, said: “Port communities are paying the price for ships running their engines 24/7 at port. Fossil fuels only seem cheap because companies offload health and climate costs onto the public. Fortunately, the solution already exists. Plugging ships into shoreside electric power would save society billions and make port cities far healthier to live in.”.

On paper, marine fuels appear less costly than drawing electricity from the port grid. However, this is largely because the associated healthcare and environmental burdens are absorbed by the local population rather than ship operators. Once these external costs are factored into energy pricing, generating power from fossil fuels at dock is twice as costly as using shore electricity.

According to recent reports, this policy gap creates a lot of planning uncertainty for EU port authorities and electricity grid operators. Without a predictable policy progressively including all vessel types, ports are disincentivised from making long-term investments in green infrastructure, says T&E.

The EU will review the regulation at the end of this year. T&E urges EU policymakers to use the AFIR review to expand shore power to all ships, batteries, and boilers, backed by national port electrification roadmaps before 2032.

Its call is echoed today in a joint letter to the European Commission from the Clean Port Cities (CPC) coalition, uniting industry, civil society, and maritime and energy stakeholders including DFDS and Green Transition Denmark, urging predictable shore power timelines for all vessels, battery charging rules, and faster grid access.

Sources indicate that ¹ The port-health research cited refers to Mei et al. (2023), “Long-term effects of air pollutants on respiratory and cardiovascular mortality in a port city along the Adriatic sea,” BMC Pulmonary Medicine.

HLTH 2026: Noom, Hims & Hers roll out peptide offerings" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

LAS VEGAS—Direct-to-consumer health companies Noom and Hims & Hers are making a play for the peptide market as the federal government loosens restrictions on compounded treatments.

The companies are betting that peptides could be the next big thing in consumer health. For Noom, the new peptide offering extends the tech giant's business beyond weight loss into the broader longevity and wellness market. Hims & Hers signaled months ago that it was ready to tap into the multi-billion-dollar peptide market.

Recent findings suggest that federal policy shifts and U.S. Food and Drug Administration enforcement discretion around compounded peptides have opened new pathways for telehealth and compounding pharmacies.

On Tuesday, Noom launched OpenRx as a separate peptide and preventive health brand. At launch, OpenRx offers two injectable options: sermorelin, a peptide frequently prescribed for muscle support, and NAD+, a coenzyme frequently prescribed for energy. OpenRx also offers two oral dissolvable tablet options: the first formulation combines the peptides PT-141 and oxytocin with tadalafil to support sexual health. The second ODT formulation is the peptide oxytocin to support intimacy.

Noom says it prepares to expand into other areas including recovery, muscle health, skin, gut health and sleep. Peptides are small pieces of protein that occur naturally in the body and help control functions such as growth, healing and appetite.

“Peptides are an crucial portion of the formulary of healthy aging,” Geoff Cook, CEO of Noom, stated in a statement. “OpenRx enables our flagship Noom brand to deepen into cardiometabolic health while the fresh brand OpenRx supports patients with conditions too often neglected by traditional care models, like energy, muscle composition, skin health, sexual health, sleep, and recovery. Together, both brands support the same mission: to empower everyone, everywhere to live better longer – every day.”.

In a recent development, noom says every OpenRx prescription is written by a licensed clinician following an evaluation of the patient’s health history, goals and clinical appropriateness. Treatments are fulfilled through Noom’s U.S.-based pharmacy network, which operates under state boards of pharmacy oversight and adheres to USP compounding standards, the company said.

Recent findings suggest that noom is right now reviewing BPC-157 and TB-500 as part of its ongoing process of evaluating emerging treatments for inclusion in our formulary, Jeffrey Egler, M.D., Noom's chief medical officer, mentioned in a statement. "Each therapy offered by OpenRx is selected because our clinical team and I believe it is appropriate for improving patient health. The process involves continuous monitoring of safety-related signals, gathering the judgment of our medical directors and the medical directors of affiliated clinical networks based on years of prescribing experience with the compounds in question, ensuring a compliant and stable supply chain, sourcing of active pharmaceutical ingredients, and setting up processes for compliance with state and federal adverse event reporting guidelines," Egler said.

Online health and wellness brand Hims & Hers confirmed earlier this month it planned to roll out a peptides business. As part of the tech giant's upcoming Peptides+ specialty, released today, it plans to initially sell five U.S.-compounded peptide and longevity treatments—Sermorelin, NAD+, Glutathione, Vitamin B12 and L-Carnitine, with plans to add more peptides and therapies over time.

The company also prepares to offer U.S.-made BPC-157 and TB-500 "consistent with regulatory requirements," the company said.

Industry observers note that A survey the organization conducted in October of 2,000 adults found that more than half (55%) remarked they were interested in or curious about peptide therapies, and 40% of U.S. adults say they are interested or very interested in a telehealth offering of injectable prescription treatments, including peptides and other compounded treatments. Nearly 1 in 10 U.S. adults (9%) say they currently use peptides, not including FDA-approved peptides such as Ozempic, Wegovy and insulin, the survey found.

Sources indicate that peptides are in the spotlight due to the massive success of FDA-approved GLP-1 weight loss medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which are peptide drugs. Wellness influencers and biohackers on social media are promoting other lab-made peptides for fast-tracked healing, anti-aging and muscle growth.

In a recent development, health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has championed looser federal rules on trendy, unapproved peptide injections. In July, an FDA advisory committee recommended broader access to six unapproved peptides. The panel recommended adding these six substances to the Section 503A Bulks List, which would remove the restrictions on how they are produced by compounders, Fierce Pharma reported.

Sources indicate that stopping short of a formal declaration allowing their use, Kennedy has cleared the way for the compounding of six popular wellness peptides, Fierce Pharma reported. Under Kennedy’s "enforcement discretion policy" issued in late October, HHS will not take enforcement action against pharmacies, physicians and federal facilities compounding six specific peptides, assuming those parties meet certain specific qualifications.

But medical experts have raised safety and clinical evidence questions around unapproved or experimental compounds. The American Medical Association (AMA) publicly opposes the Trump administration’s strategy to make certain unapproved peptides more widely available for human use.

In a letter (PDF) to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the AMA pushed back what it called a "rushed" decision to permit the compounding of certain peptides because they have not been approved for safe use by the FDA.

Unproven peptides may pose serious health risks, including allergic reactions, infections, hormonal imbalances and other unexpected side effects, according to the FDA website.

Industry observers note that "We should not bypass the science and put patients at risk by making them guinea pigs for unapproved drugs," AMA President Willie Underwood III, M.D., mentioned in a statement. "If these substances are safe and effective, the evidence should demonstrate that through the FDA’s rigorous review process.".

Hims & Hers' peptide therapy program provides a "clinically guided, personalized plan" for consumers "backed by a licensed provider who understands these therapies," according to Anant Vinjamoori, M.D., chief medical officer of the Hims brand.

Hims & Hers wants to "set the standard" for peptide therapy and offer consistency in the quality of the products, Vinjamoori said in an interview on the sidelines of the HLTH conference this week.

"If you think about what we have to bring to the table with our scale and resources, I would argue there's no one better equipped to do it than us," Vinjamoori stated.

Hims & Hers has invested in its supply chain and expanded its domestic manufacturing facilities. In 2025, the organization acquired a Menlo Park peptide facility to run API validation and stability testing to support its specialized peptide offerings.

Recent findings suggest that "That's why we're investing in our supply chain and doing a lot of the hard work that, frankly, is not the fastest path to making these available. There are pharmacies that are already out there that are making these available, and there are companies out there that will simply just plug into those pharmacies and service patients. But there are inconsistencies," he noted.

Industry observers note that until now, getting these types of medications has often meant relying on unreliable and unregulated online sellers, or a high-cost longevity clinic, Hims & Hers executives noted. Hims & Hers' peptides offering gives consumers more accessible care, "backed by real medical leadership and with consistent clinical oversight," the company said in a press release.

Hims & Hers believes its scale gives it an opportunity and responsibility to help build the evidence base around peptides, using growing patient interest not just to expand access but to better understand how the treatments can be used safely and effectively, Vinjamoori stated.

According to recent reports, expanding into peptides fits with Hims & Hers' ongoing focus on personalized health, he noted. "We started with sexual health, moved on to hair loss, and then we've continued to broaden into other categories such as hormone replacement, GLP-1s, and now peptides, and many others to come. And the common theme in all of this is that we're talking about helping people accomplish a specific goal that they have. We're not talking about curing a disease or treating a disease per se," he said. "We're talking about, 'Hey, there's something you want to do in your life that you're not able to do right now. Let's help you figure out how we can put together a plan to help you accomplish that.".

Recent findings suggest that "This is a big part of the future of medicine itself," Vinjamoori added. "It's been the missing part of the equation, where we've been very focused on treating and responding to disease, but not as much, not just on prevention, but really on helping people use their health as an asset and as a tool to help them accomplish what they want in life.".

With Hims & Hers' peptide therapy offering, consumers start with a clinical visit with a licensed provider that includes a comprehensive intake of health history and goals. The manufacturer said a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies assesses each individual and, if appropriate, tailors a personalized protocol to their needs.

Hims & Hers treatments are compounded in the U.S. and dispensed directly by licensed, U.S. pharmacies regulated by state boards of pharmacy and "held to rigorous quality and safety standards," the company said.

The buzz around peptides ties into consumers' growing interest in taking control of their health "driven by the cultural zeitgeist moment," Vinjamoori told Fierce Healthcare.

Recent findings suggest that "There's a variety of different factors that catalyze that. I think the COVID-19 pandemic catalyzed a lot of it for a variety of reasons. I think you see accelerations in biotechnology where people now see something like GLP-1s that can help with a problem that seemed intractable before. I think people are now interested in figuring out what is the range of solutions that could help me. I also think peptides represent something that has a lot of promise, a lot of excitement," he remarked.

It has been revealed that "But there are also some cautions that we need to take as well. Something we think a lot about is how do we meet this moment of excitement and enthusiasm with some degree of rigor and guardrails," Vinjamoori stated.

According to recent reports, "It starts with the product itself. How do we ensure the quality? The compounds are of the highest quality and are compounded in the most rigorous way, made available in the most rigorous way. That's why we are trying to have as much oversight as we can into the full process of making these available," he noted.

He asserted that informed consent and transparency with consumers are critical. "I've spent a lot of time with the team to make sure that we understand that people have this enthusiasm, but we need to make sure that they understand what they're getting into. There is a difference between this and FDA-approved therapies," he said.

Industry observers note that "Sometimes people should try the standard of care before they engage with some of these things, and so we want to make sure we have these conversations with people openly and honestly. But at the same time, we also want to respect their choice," he added.

According to recent reports, hims & Hers Peptides+ is available with its Care+ program that gives customers access to twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress, unlimited support and ongoing check-ins from a dedicated care team. Customers can also message providers trained in peptide therapy 24/7 with any questions. The Hims Men’s panel includes at-home blood collection and access to lab tests that provide insights across 22 biomarkers, including testosterone, vitamin D, and cholesterol. The Hers Women’s panel tests 22 biomarkers across hormones, vitamins, and heart health.

Slate Thinks 205 Miles Is More Than Enough Range

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that slate Auto is in a strange spot.
  • Industry observers note that it makes sense why the Slate has such a shoddy range, even compared to its competition.
  • In a recent development, still, Slate feels 205 miles is really all the average American needs from a vehicle like its truck, the cheapest EV and pickup for sale in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that slate Auto is in a strange spot. Yes, with a starting price of $26,400, including destination, the two-door pickup truck it's selling is cheap compared to the competition, but it also lacks basic features like power windows and a radio at that price. With options that'll make the truck more livable for everyday use, prices will quickly climb. No matter which options they choose, they'll still be saddled with the same 205 miles of range. Even though that's quite meager by today's standards, Slate feels that's more than enough to win over customers.

Industry observers note that it makes sense why the Slate has such a shoddy range, even compared to its competition. The battery is the single most expensive part of an electric vehicle, so an automaker looking to make a cheap EV will use a smaller battery. There's a view that Slate's approach could work for folks who are already comfortable with EVs, but it might not translate for those more accustomed to what gas-powered vehicles offer, according to Automotive News. There's also the issue that similarly priced rivals will offer more range on base models, and they usually have the option of extended-range batteries.

In a recent development, still, Slate feels 205 miles is really all the average American needs from a vehicle like its truck, the cheapest EV and pickup for sale in the U.S. To be fair, it's also the smallest pickup in the U.S. — about two feet shorter than a Ford Maverick. In a marketing email sent earlier this month, Slate said 205 miles is "more than [many people] need each day." That's sort of fair, because according to a 2024 survey done by AAA, the average American drives about 31 miles per day, meaning that from full to empty, you'd only need to charge the Slate about once a week. Of course, no one actually drives like that, and the range will never actually be 205 miles, but we can't really account for that.

Sources indicate that slate isn't the only company offering an EV with less-than-stellar range. The Kia EV3 compact crossover, which starts at $31,385, comes as standard with 221 miles of range. While the starting prices are far different, the EV3 comes with a lot more from the get-go. To get the Slate to a comparable place, you've got to add a bed kit that brings in seats and a roof — giving the Slate "crossover" a $31,400 base price, according to AutoNews. It'll still be missing plenty of other things at that price, like a radio and electric windows.

In any case, Kia doesn't expect this low-range EV3 to be a big seller — capturing just 3 to 5% of its sales. The higher Wind trim, with its 321 miles of range and $36,485 starting price, is expected to be the volume seller with about 60% of sales. That sort of speaks to Slate's problem. It seems like folks would rather pay the extra money to not have to worry about range anxiety or charging up their cars as often.

In reality, the EV3 isn't a direct competitor to the Slate, but Ford's yet-to-be-unveiled Fathom pickup is. It's expected to have a standard battery with around 250 miles of range and an optional battery with over 300 miles, Automotive News reports. Despite the fact it range-mogs the Slate, its starting price will come in at $29,945, including shipping, and it'll be an actual vehicle with the sort of modern luxuries and conveniences you'd expect in today's day and age.

I'm not saying that the Slate is dead on arrival by any means, but I do think the Jeff Bezos-backed company is really, really hoping that there are a lot of Quirked Up Individuals out there who will fall for the proletariat virtual signals of crank windows, no radio, a key you've got to insert and no screen while also paying a price that doesn't really connect with that reality. I'm not sure they're out there.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cadillac’s three-row electric SUV just got a little more expensive. The 2027 Cadillac Vistiq now starts at over $80,000.

The Vistiq sits between the massive Escalade IQ and Lyriq as a “mini Escalade,” if you will, offering three rows of seating, but in a smaller, more affordable package.

Just a month ago, the 2027 Cadillac Vistiq was available starting at $79,495, but GM quietly raised prices.

In a recent development, as GM Authority uncovered on Cadillac’s website, prices for the base 2027 Vistiq Luxury are now listed from $80,395, or $900 more than last month. In fact, the Luxury, Premium Luxury, and Platinum models are all $900 more, while the Sport trim got a $1,000 price increase.

While $900 won’t break the bank on a luxury three-row SUV, the cheapest 2027 Cadillac Vistiq Luxury trim now starts at over $80,000.

Like all 2027 GM electric vehicles, the Vistiq now has a built-in NACS charge port, so you don’t need a separate adapter to use at Tesla Superchargers.

The 2027 Cadillac Vistiq is available in four trims: Luxury, Sport, Premium Luxury, and Platinum. All are powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain that delivers a combined 615 hp and 650 lb-ft of torque.

Cadillac’s three-row electric SUV uses a 102 kWh battery, offering an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 305 miles on a single charge.

All trims come with a 33″ Horizon Display, Power driver and front passenger massage seats, a premium 23-speaker AKG Studio audio system, and a Power SkyGlass roof as standard.

At 205.6″ long, 79.7″ wide, and 71″ tall, with a 121.8″ wheelbase, the Vistiq is slightly longer but shorter than the Rivian R1S.

While Cadillac raised prices on the three-row 2027 Vistiq this month, the 2027 Optiq, Cadillac’s most affordable EV, got a bit cheaper.

HLTH 2026: Viz.ai executive shares lessons from effort to expand AI adoption at rural hospitals" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

It’s been almost seven months since artificial intelligence disease detection and care coordination platform Viz.ai entered into a partnership with the National Rural Health Association (NRHA).

The partnership aims to help rural healthcare leaders better understand and implement AI tools across systems. That's been a personal and professional passion of Viz.ai Chief Clinical Officer Andrew Ibrahim, M.D., who discussed with Fierce Healthcare at HLTH his key takeaways from the collaboration thus far and forward-looking goals as it approaches its one-year mark.

In a recent development, ibrahim said that the two organizations have done three educational events for rural health systems since the partnership kicked off in April. These series aim to show rural health administrators the specifics of AI—and whether they should adopt it, he said.

He noted there’s “sometimes a very major mismatch” when smaller rural health systems onboard multiple vendors.

“We've learned [that] many rural hospitals don't have the IT expertise and infrastructure to adopt some of these tools, and so it's actually been a force function to strengthen their hub spoke relationships,” Ibrahim said.

Strengthening these relationships, according to Ibrahim, has been key.

According to recent reports, “It's actually been beautiful to see the hub-spoke relationship strengthened with the AI tool as the conduit,” Ibrahim said. “And it gives them a reason to interact more, and a way for the rural hospitals to strengthen their capabilities.”.

He continued, “there's an authenticity about the moment where it's like ‘Yeah, we do need to help each other out.’ We're all kind of figuring it out as we go.”.

In addition to the educational series, Ibrahim said frameworks are in development to aid rural health systems in navigating, implementing and deploying AI—which will be built into a toolkit.

One of Ibrahim’s personal goals for the one-year mark of the partnership is to ensure any rural health administrator can understand what an AI tool is when pitched.

“I think that would be a huge milestone,” he stated. “Getting to 100% of hospitals at year one would be ideal—probably unrealistic, but that's probably the ultimate goal.”.

And when it comes to metrics for measuring the collaboration, Ibrahim said he's looking for numbers that show participants are “keeping more care local” and retaining their workforces.

“It would be great to be able to connect the dots [and understand whether] adoption of an AI tool give[s] rural clinicians confidence, enthusiasm, willingness to stay in their community as opposed to dropping the services and moving back,” he remarked.

Another initiative from Viz that has “disproportionate benefit in rural communities,” according to Ibrahim, is its new partnership with Wolters Kluwer Health to integrate the Viz.ai One platform into UpToDate Expert AI.

“I'm pretty excited about being able to bring their level of clinical decision support into our rural hospitals,” he mentioned.

  • It has been revealed that the new law, which takes effect on February 27, 2027, is part of a new section of the state's General Business Law, according to Spectrum News.
  • In a recent development, hochul called the practice a "deceptive business model," according to CBS 6 Albany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in-vehicle subscriptions are pretty universally maligned among car owners. Most folks don't like the feeling of having to pay every month for features their cars were supposed to come with, and now Fresh York State is doing something about it. Governor Kathy Hochul just signed a bill that bars automakers, dealers and their agents from selling subscriptions for features that are already installed.

It has been revealed that the new law, which takes effect on February 27, 2027, is part of a new section of the state's General Business Law, according to Spectrum News. You can read the law for yourself here. It lays out fairly simple ground rules when it comes to subscriptions dealers or manufacturers can offer you: The feature must use hardware already in the car when it was bought or leased, and it must keep working without continual costs or support from the automaker or a third party. Those two things pretty much bring an end to crap like subscription-based heated seats and alike. It also is supposed to cover hands-off driving systems and enhanced navigation. Basically, once the hardware is physically in the car and the manufacturer isn't paying anything for you to use it, they can't then charge you. OEMs will also not be able to charge for software updates that fix safety defects.

In a recent development, hochul called the practice a "deceptive business model," according to CBS 6 Albany. She also told automakers to keep their hands out of New Yorkers' wallets. It passed through the New York State Senate 57-3.

As with all good things, there are some exceptions. First of all, your lease or payment blueprint doesn't count as a subscription, so don't even try it, slick.

The law also doesn't apply to navigation updates, infotainment features, satellite radio, in-vehicle WiFi, telematics, roadside assistance or "vehicle-connected services" that rely on cellular data or other networks, according to Motor1. It also exempts software-dependent driver assistance features, like Tesla's Full Self-Driving or GM's Super Cruise.

Sources indicate that I know what you're thinking. Didn't I just mention that hands-free driving systems are covered? Well, yes, but subscriptions tied to software and data are likely to survive, while hardware-only features are the real targets. Automakers will almost certainly make the argument that things like FSD and Super Cruise are "connected" or "software-dependent.".

According to recent reports, one prime example of what this bill aims to get rid of is BMW keeping things like a 360-degree camera behind a paywall. That hardware is already built into the car, and, as we reported, it doesn't require a data connection to operate. It's the same thing with features like high-beam assist and remote start, so I imagine it'll be hard for BMW and other companies with similar schemes to argue that these are "connected." I mean, these are the same people who argue that buyers actually want subscriptions, which is certainly not true.

In any case, violators will face civil penalties of up to $250 per point-of-sale for each violation, though it's not clear exactly how that'll be counted. It's not clear if other states are going to follow suit, but here's hoping.
